name: M01 - Introduction to Stock Markets
type:LABEL: Module
summary: Why invest, asset classes, market ecosystem (SEBI, brokers, depositories, clearing), IPO lifecycle, how stocks move, returns math, indices, jargon, order types, settlement, corporate actions, macro events, developing a point of view.

name: Investing
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Deploying surplus cash into asset classes to fight inflation, create wealth and meet financial goals.
facts: [{"Idle cash loses to inflation; example": "Rs 20k/month surplus held as cash for 20 yrs ~ Rs 1.7 Cr vs ~Rs 4.26 Cr invested at 12%."}, "Corpus is highly sensitive to rate of return; small rate changes have large compounding impact.", "Reasons to invest - fight inflation, create wealth, meet life's financial aspirations."]

name: Asset Class
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: A category of investment with particular risk and return characteristics - fixed income, equity, real estate, commodities (precious metals).
facts: ["Fixed income - limited risk to principal, interest paid periodically, capital returned at maturity; ~8-11% (2014).", "Equity - no capital guarantee; Indian equities ~14-15% CAGR over 15 years; best companies >20% CAGR.", "Real estate - rental income + capital appreciation; large outlay, illiquid, no official return metric.", "Bullion (gold/silver) - ~8% CAGR over 20 years; via jewelry or ETFs.", "Risk and return go hand in hand.", "Fixed income can lose in real terms - a 9% FD with 10% inflation = -1% real return."]

name: Fixed Income Instruments
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Instruments with limited principal risk paying interest (FDs, G-secs, PSU bonds like HUDCO/NHAI, corporate bonds).

name: Equity (Shares)
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Part-ownership of a publicly listed company traded on BSE/NSE; highest long-run return, no capital guarantee.
facts: ["A share represents part ownership; owner entitled to dividends, bonus, splits, rights, voting.", "Buying a share means taking the same kind of risk as the promoter, scaled by holding."]

name: Asset Allocation
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Allocating money across asset classes based on risk appetite.
facts: ["Young professional example - ~70% equity, 20% precious metals, 10% fixed income.", "Retired example - ~80% fixed income, 10% equity, 10% precious metals."]

name: Stock Exchange (NSE / BSE)
type:LABEL: Participant
summary: Electronic marketplace matching buyers and sellers; India's two main exchanges are NSE and BSE.
facts: ["Exists electronically; accessed only via a registered stock broker.", "Exchange's order-matching algorithm pairs orders; seller can be one or many counterparties.", "Different opinions make a market - a trade needs an opposing view.", "Regional exchanges are being phased out."]

name: Market Participants
type:LABEL: Participant
summary: Domestic retail, NRI/OCI, domestic institutions (e.g. LIC), domestic AMCs (mutual funds), Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs).
facts: ["FIIs transact large amounts so their activity moves market sentiment.", "Everyone's agenda is to make profitable transactions; greed/fear drive unfair practices, hence regulation."]

name: Foreign Institutional Investors (FII/FPI)
type:LABEL: Participant
summary: Foreign corporates/funds/individuals investing in India in large size; flows impact sentiment.
bot_use: Track FII net buy/sell flows as a sentiment input.

name: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)
type:LABEL: Participant
summary: India's securities market regulator - develops exchanges, protects retail investors, regulates participants and intermediaries.
facts: ["Ensures exchanges, brokers, corporates act fairly; prevents manipulation by large investors; protects retail.", "Regulates CRAs (CRISIL, ICRA, CARE), debenture trustees, depositories (NSDL, CDSL), DPs, FIIs, merchant bankers, AMCs, PMS (min Rs 25 lakh at the time), brokers/sub-brokers.", "Has final say on whether a company can go public.", "Publishes entity rules in its 'Legal Framework' section."]

name: Stock Broker
type:LABEL: Participant
summary: SEBI-registered trading member of an exchange; your gateway to markets via a trading account.
facts: ["Services - market access, margins, dealing/software support, contract notes, fund transfers, back office.", "Access modes - call & trade, web, trading terminal (e.g. Zerodha Kite).", "Charges brokerage for services."]

name: Trading Account
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Account with a broker used to buy/sell securities; linked to a DEMAT account and exactly one bank account.
facts: ["Only one bank account (in your own name) can be linked to a trading account at a time."]

name: DEMAT Account
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Electronic vault holding dematerialised shares, maintained by a depository (NSDL or CDSL) through a Depository Participant.
facts: ["Paper certificates converted to electronic form post-1996 ('dematerialisation').", "Only two depositories in India - NSDL and CDSL.", "You open a DEMAT account through a DP (agent of the depository)."]

name: Depository (NSDL / CDSL) and Depository Participant
type:LABEL: Participant
summary: NSDL and CDSL hold securities electronically; DPs (banks/brokers) are their agents.

name: Clearing Corporation (NSCCL / ICCL)
type:LABEL: Participant
summary: Exchange subsidiaries that guarantee settlement - match debits/credits and prevent default.

name: Company Funding Lifecycle
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Seed (promoter + angels) -> Series A (VC) -> Series B -> Series C (Private Equity) -> IPO; valuation rises as revenue/profit validate business.
facts: ["Angel investors invest pre-revenue, take maximum risk (as much as promoter), small amounts.", "Seed fund becomes initial share capital in the company's bank account.", "Face value - nominal denomination per share (e.g. Rs 10).", "Authorized shares - total shares available; issued shares are a subset allotted to holders.", "VC invests early-stage, smaller amounts; PE invests large sums in mature firms and takes board seats.", "Capex can be funded by internal accruals, equity (VC/PE/IPO) or debt (loans/bonds).", "Implied valuation = investment / stake (e.g. 7 Cr for 14% => 50 Cr).", "Credible prior VC/PE rounds are a quality signal for IPO companies."]

name: Capital Expenditure (Capex)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Spending to expand/improve the business (plants, stores, capacity).

name: Face Value (Par Value)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Fixed nominal denomination of a share; dividends and splits are referenced to it.
facts: ["Dividend % = dividend per share / face value (Infosys Rs 42 on FV 5 => 840%)."]

name: Initial Public Offering (IPO)
type:LABEL: Process
summary: First offer of a company's shares to the public, moving it from private to listed (primary -> secondary market).
bot_use: Subscription multiple and anchor/VC pedigree are pre-listing sentiment features; listing day = start of secondary trading.
caveats: ["Investors should read the DRHP; some companies list without healthy prior funding rounds."]
facts: ["Reasons - raise capex funds, spread promoter risk, exit for early investors, reward employees via ESOPs, visibility.", "Sequence - appoint merchant banker -> registration statement to SEBI -> SEBI nod -> DRHP -> road show -> price band -> book building -> closure -> listing day.", "DRHP contents - IPO size, shares offered, use of funds with timeline, business model, financials, MD&A, risks, management.", "Book building - investors bid within the price band; listing price usually where max bids received.", "Undersubscription signals negative sentiment; oversubscription Nx = bids/shares offered.", "Green shoe option - over-allotment up to ~15% extra shares if oversubscribed.", "Fixed price IPO has no band; cut-off price = final discovered price within band.", "Most Indian IPOs follow book building."]

name: Merchant Banker (BRLM / Lead Manager)
type:LABEL: Participant
summary: Assists IPO - due diligence, DRHP, underwriting, price band, road shows, appointing registrars/bankers.

name: Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Public IPO disclosure document with business, financials, use of proceeds, risks and management.

name: Primary vs Secondary Market
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Primary market = IPO bidding/issuance; secondary market = trading on exchange after listing.

name: Follow-on Public Offer (FPO)
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Post-listing public issue of fresh (dilutive) shares via DRHP + book building, used to fund new projects; rare since OFS (2012).

name: Offer for Sale (OFS)
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Exchange window for promoters to sell existing shares (no new shares) at/above a floor price; also to meet minimum public shareholding.
facts: ["Only top 200 companies by market cap may use OFS (per source).", "Allotment settled to demat T+1.", "PSU minimum public shareholding 25% example."]

name: What Moves Stock Prices
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Prices move on news/events (company, industry, economy) and expectations, and on demand-supply imbalance even without news.
bot_use: News/event sentiment and sector contagion features; liquidity filter - illiquid names don't respond.
facts: ["Good news -> buyers lift offers repeatedly -> price rally (Infosys new CEO example 3000->3016 in 5 min).", "Industry-wide news (e.g. NASSCOM cutting IT budget outlook) hits all sector stocks.", "Large liquid stocks move even without news; illiquid small caps may barely move.", "Macro/political events (e.g. 2014 election) move the whole market."]

name: Holding Period
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Period you intend to hold a position - minutes to forever.

name: Absolute Return
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Percentage gain irrespective of time.
conditions: {"use_when": "holding period <= 1 year"}

name: Compounded Annual Growth Rate (CAGR)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Annualised growth rate over multiple years.
conditions: {"use_when": "holding period > 1 year"}
facts: ["Compare returns only on an annualised basis; 17.16% in 6 months ~ 34.32% annualised (simple)."]

name: Trader and Investor Types
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Traders (short view, unbiased long/short) vs investors (multi-year holding).
facts: ["Day trader - opens and closes intraday, no overnight risk, ~5-6 stocks/day.", "Scalper - very large size, very short hold, tiny per-share profit (e.g. 10,000 sh x Rs 0.10).", "Swing trader - holds days to weeks.", "Growth investor - companies growing on industry/macro trends.", "Value investor - good companies beaten down by short-term sentiment (L&T 1200->690->1440).", "Traders and investors differ on risk-taking ability and holding period."]

name: Stock Market Index (Nifty / Sensex)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Basket of large, liquid stocks acting as a barometer of the market/economy; Nifty (NSE) and Sensex (BSE).
bot_use: Benchmark strategy returns against Nifty; use index as regime/market-trend filter; hedge with index futures.
facts: ["Uses - information, benchmarking performance, trading (via derivatives), portfolio hedging.", "Index up = participants optimistic about future; down = pessimistic.", "Weights by free-float market capitalisation; stocks must keep qualifying or get replaced.", "A stock's weight is the share of index movement attributable to it (e.g. ITC 7.6% in 2014).", "Sectoral indices - Bank Nifty, CNX IT etc.", "Majority of traders trade the index."]

name: Sectoral Index
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Index of a specific sector (Bank Nifty, CNX IT) reflecting sector sentiment.

name: Free Float Market Capitalisation
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Market value of shares available for trading; basis of Indian index weights.

name: Bull / Bear Market
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Bullish = expecting rise (index rising period = bull market); bearish = expecting fall.

name: Trend
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: General market direction and its strength - bullish, bearish or sideways.

name: 52-Week High / Low and All-Time High / Low
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Highest/lowest traded price over last 52 weeks (or since listing).
conditions: {"bullish_hint": "close >= max(high, 252 sessions)", "bearish_hint": "close <= min(low, 252 sessions)"}
bot_use: Breakout/momentum filter.
facts: ["Many believe a 52-week high indicates a bullish trend ahead and a 52-week low a bearish trend."]

name: Long Position
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Buy first, sell later; bullish; profit if price rises.

name: Short Position (Shorting)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Sell first (borrowed), buy back later; bearish; profit if price falls, loss if it rises.
facts: ["Exchange handles borrowing/returning in the background.", "Multi-day shorts are best done in the derivatives market (equity cash shorts are intraday)."]

name: Square Off
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Closing an existing position - sell to close a long, buy to close a short (not a new short/long).

name: Intraday Position
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Position initiated with intent to square off the same day.

name: OHLC and Volume
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Open, high, low, close prices of a period; volume = total shares transacted.
facts: ["Open is fixed once set; high and low update as price trades intraday."]

name: Market Segments
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Capital market (equity 'EQ', preference shares, warrants, ETFs), Futures & Options (leveraged derivatives), Wholesale Debt Market (G-secs, T-bills, bonds).

name: Trading Terminal / Market Watch
type:LABEL: Product
summary: Broker software to view quotes (LTP, % change, OHLC, volume), market depth and place/modify orders.
facts: ["Order book tracks orders (open/completed/rejected) and allows modify/cancel; trade book shows executed trades.", "Market depth (snap quote) shows top 5 bid/ask levels with order counts and quantities."]

name: Order Types (Limit, Market, SL, SL-M)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Limit = specific price (may not fill); Market = immediate at available prices (price uncertainty); SL/SL-M = passive stop that activates at trigger price.
conditions: {"long_stop": {"trigger_price": "> stop_price", "activates_when": "ltp <= trigger_price"}}
bot_use: Prefer limit orders to control slippage; place SL/SL-M orders immediately after entry.
facts: ["Market orders walk the book and fill at multiple prices; dangerous for active traders in fast markets.", "Stop loss is passive until trigger price is crossed; for a long, trigger is set slightly above the SL limit price (e.g. trigger 256, SL 255)."]

name: Product Types (CNC, MIS, NRML)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: CNC = delivery (hold in demat); MIS = intraday margin product (auto square-off); NRML = normal (carry-forward F&O).

name: MIS (Margin Intraday Square-off)
type:LABEL: Product
summary: Intraday leveraged product squared off same day.

name: Bid, Ask and Market Depth
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Bid = best prices buyers will pay; ask/offer = prices sellers demand; depth shows top 5 levels each side.
bot_use: Estimate slippage by walking the depth for order size; use bid/ask totals as order-flow imbalance feature.
facts: ["Lowest ask has highest priority for sellers; highest bid for buyers (price priority).", "A market buy of 10 shares with 2 @ best ask fills across several levels and moves LTP.", "Understanding order stacking is critical for intraday traders."]

name: Clearing and Settlement (T+2 per source)
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Buy on T day - funds + charges debited T; shares credited to demat end of T+2 (per source); sale proceeds credited T+2.
caveats: ["Source describes T+2; India moved to T+1 settlement in 2023 - verify current cycle."]
facts: ["Contract note issued on T day for all trades.", "BTST (buy today sell tomorrow) sells shares not yet in demat - risk of short delivery, esp. in B-group/illiquid stocks.", "Sold shares are blocked immediately."]

name: BTST / ATST
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Selling shares bought the previous day before they reach demat.
caveats: ["Short-delivery/auction risk especially in illiquid and B-group stocks; avoid unless risk understood."]

name: Contract Note
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Legal record of trades and charges issued by broker on trade day.

name: Transaction Charges (brokerage, STT, exchange fees, GST, SEBI fees, stamp duty)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Costs on every trade - brokerage, Securities Transaction Tax, exchange transaction charges, service tax/GST, SEBI turnover fee.
bot_use: Always deduct full round-trip costs in backtests; costs dominate high-frequency strategies.
caveats: ["Rates in source are dated; use current schedule."]

name: Corporate Actions
type:LABEL: Event
summary: Board-initiated, shareholder-approved actions that change the stock - dividends, bonus, split, rights, buyback.
bot_use: Adjust historical prices for splits/bonuses; flag ex-dates to avoid false gaps in signals.

name: Dividend
type:LABEL: Event
summary: Distribution of profits (or reserves) per share, expressed as % of face value; interim or final.
bot_use: Price drops roughly by dividend amount on ex-date - adjust backtests; dividend arbitrage awareness.
facts: ["Not mandatory; can be paid from reserves even in a loss year.", "Timeline - declaration date (AGM) -> ex-dividend date -> record date (~30 days after declaration); stock is cum-dividend until ex-date.", "Ex-date is set ~2 business days before record date due to T+2; buy before ex-date to be entitled.", "High payout makes sense when growth opportunities are exhausted."]

name: Bonus Issue
type:LABEL: Event
summary: Free shares from reserves in a fixed ratio (e.g. 2:1 = 2 new per 1 held); share count rises, price adjusts, value unchanged.
facts: ["Done to improve retail affordability/liquidity when share price is high."]

name: Stock Split
type:LABEL: Event
summary: Face value split (e.g. FV 10 -> 5); shares multiply, price divides, market cap unchanged.

name: Rights Issue
type:LABEL: Event
summary: Fresh capital raised from existing shareholders in proportion to holding (e.g. 1:4) at a discount; dilutive.
caveats: ["Don't be swayed by discount; if market price < rights price", "buy in market instead."]

name: Share Buyback
type:LABEL: Event
summary: Company buys back its own shares, reducing share count.
facts: ["Reasons - improve EPS, consolidate promoter stake, prevent takeover, signal confidence, support price.", "Usually positive for share price."]

name: Key Macro Events
type:LABEL: Event
summary: Monetary policy, inflation, IIP, PMI, Budget and quarterly earnings move markets.

name: RBI Monetary Policy (Repo, Reverse Repo, CRR)
type:LABEL: Event
summary: RBI balances growth vs inflation via key rates; reviewed periodically (quarterly per source).
bot_use: Event-day volatility regime; sector rotation on rate decisions.
facts: ["Repo - rate at which RBI lends to banks; higher = costlier borrowing, slower growth; markets dislike hikes.", "Reverse repo - rate at which RBI borrows from banks; hike tightens money supply.", "CRR - share of deposits banks must keep with RBI; higher CRR drains liquidity.", "Rate-sensitive sectors react first - banks, autos, housing finance, real estate, metals.", "Higher rates curb inflation; lower rates tend to raise inflation."]

name: Interest Rates
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Cost of money; drives borrowing, growth, inflation, bond prices, currency and futures pricing.

name: Inflation (CPI / WPI)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Sustained rise in general prices measured by WPI (wholesale) and CPI (retail); MOSPI publishes CPI ~2nd week monthly.
facts: ["High inflation is a bad signal for markets.", "CPI is what matters to consumers."]

name: Index of Industrial Production (IIP)
type:LABEL: Event
summary: Monthly industrial production index by MOSPI; rising = positive for markets; low IIP pressures RBI to cut rates.

name: Purchasing Managers Index (PMI)
type:LABEL: Event
summary: Survey-based manufacturing/services activity index.
conditions: {"expansion": "pmi > 50", "contraction": "pmi < 50", "no_change": "pmi == 50"}

name: Union Budget
type:LABEL: Event
summary: Annual finance ministry presentation (around Feb 1 now; last week of Feb per source) with policy/tax changes; strong market reactions.

name: Quarterly Earnings Announcement
type:LABEL: Event
summary: Listed companies report quarterly revenue, expenses, taxes, profit and sometimes guidance.
conditions: {"signal": "sign(actual - consensus)", "in_line": "flat_to_negative_bias"}
bot_use: Earnings-surprise strategies; avoid holding through results unless intended; widen stops/IV crush awareness.
facts: ["Price reacts to actual vs street expectation - beat = up, miss = down, in-line = flat with negative bias.", "Indian quarters - Q1 Apr-Jun (results ~July), Q2 Jul-Sep (~Oct), Q3 Oct-Dec (~Jan), Q4 Jan-Mar (~Apr); Infosys usually reports first."]

name: Point of View (POV) and Instrument Selection
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Success requires a researched directional view (via FA, TA, quant) plus choosing the right instrument to express it.
bot_use: Map signal horizon/conviction to instrument - equity for long-term, futures for short-term directional, options for capped-risk/event trades.
facts: ["Methods - Fundamental, Technical, Quantitative analysis, outside views (avoid relying on outside views).", "Long-term very bullish -> delivery equity; short-term (1 week) bullish -> futures; bullish with limited risk -> options.", "Bullish can be expressed via spot, futures, calls, puts combos or synthetic positions."]

name: M02 - Technical Analysis
type:LABEL: Module
summary: TA assumptions, chart types, timeframes, 16 candlestick patterns with entry/stop rules, support & resistance, volume, moving averages, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, Fibonacci, Dow Theory, range breakouts, flags, RRR, the 6-point checklist, scanning process, scalping, and supplementary indicators (ADX, Alligator, Aroon, ATR, ATR bands, Supertrend, VWAP).

name: Technical Analysis (TA)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Research technique identifying trading opportunities from market participants' actions (price/volume) visualised as charts and patterns.
facts: ["Best for short-term trades (minutes to weeks); use FA for long-term investments; FA investors can use TA to time entries/exits.", "Expect small but consistent profits from frequent short-term trades, not windfalls.", "Cut losses quickly; do not hold losing TA trades hoping to recover.", "Applicable to any asset with OHLCV time series - equities, commodities, FX, fixed income; indicators work identically across assets.", "TA vs FA is not a contest; prudent traders learn both.", "Assumptions - (1) markets discount everything, (2) 'how' matters more than 'why', (3) price moves in trends, (4) history tends to repeat itself.", "History repeats only when the same set of factors recurs (factor addendum).", "Indian market hours 9:15 to 15:30."]

name: Closing Price is Most Important
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Close is the final evaluation of the period, the reference for next session and the basis of most indicators; close > open = positive day.

name: Chart Types (Line, Bar, Candlestick)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Line chart plots closes only (trend view, little info); bar chart shows OHLC with left tick open/right tick close (hard to read); Japanese candlestick is the default.
facts: ["Bar length (high-low) is the range.", "Candlesticks originated with rice trader Homma Munehisa (18th c.), popularised in the West by Steve Nison."]

name: Japanese Candlestick Anatomy
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Real body connects open and close; upper shadow to high, lower shadow to low; bullish (blue/green) if close > open, bearish (red) if close < open.
formula: {"body": "abs(close - open)", "upper_shadow": "high - max(open, close)", "lower_shadow": "min(open, close) - low", "range": "high - low", "bullish": "close > open", "bearish": "close < open"}
facts: ["Long body = strong buying/selling; short body = little activity."]

name: Timeframes and Look-back Period
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Monthly (12 candles/yr), weekly (52), daily (~252), intraday 30m (~12/day), 15m (25/day), 5m (75/day); choose to filter information from noise.
facts: ["Long-term investors - weekly/monthly; swing/positional - EOD; scalpers - 1m/5m.", "Higher timeframe signals are more reliable (15m engulfing > 5m engulfing).", "Look-back - swing trader 6-12 months; scalper ~5 days; S&R plotting at least 2 years (or 3-6 months for short-term S&R, 12-18 months for long-term S&R).", "Beginners should start with positional/swing trades (hold a few days), not day trading."]

name: Candlestick Trading Rules (3 assumptions)
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: (1) Buy strength, sell weakness - buy on a blue day, sell on a red day; (2) be flexible but quantify and verify deviations; (3) look for a prior trend - bullish patterns need a prior downtrend, bearish need a prior uptrend.
conditions: {"confirmation_long": "next_day.close > next_day.open", "confirmation_short": "next_day.close < next_day.open", "tradable_range": "0.01 <= (high - low)/close <= 0.10", "stop_long": "min(low over pattern candles)", "stop_short": "max(high over pattern candles)"}
bot_use: Implement pattern detectors with tolerance params; require prior trend filter; enter at close of signal bar (aggressive) or next bar close with colour confirmation (conservative).
facts: ["Marubozu is the only pattern exempt from the prior-trend rule.", "Each pattern carries built-in entry and stop-loss; targets come from S&R.", "Risk taker enters at ~3:20 PM on the pattern's last day after validating; risk averse enters next day near close only if that day confirms (blue for long, red for short).", "The more days in a pattern, the better to enter on the pattern day itself (stars - enter on P3).", "Long stop = lowest low of the pattern; short stop = highest high of the pattern.", "Avoid trading candles with range < 1% (too subdued) or > 10% (stop too deep).", "Once in a trade, do nothing until target or stop hits (trailing stops allowed)."]

name: Prior Trend Requirement
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Reversal patterns are valid only after an opposing trend; a perfect hammer without a prior downtrend is not a pattern.
conditions: {"prior_downtrend_proxy": "close[t-1] < close[t-1-n] (e.g. n=5..10) or close below falling short EMA", "prior_uptrend_proxy": "close[t-1] > close[t-1-n] or close above rising short EMA"}
caveats: ["Source defines prior trend visually; the proxies are implementation choices."]

name: Bullish Marubozu
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Long blue candle with no shadows (open = low, close = high) showing buying at every price; bullish regardless of prior trend.
conditions: {"identify": "close > open and abs(open - low) <= tol*high and abs(high - close) <= tol*high", "tol_example": "ACC 0.17% deviation accepted", "entry": "near close of marubozu (risk taker) or next day close if next day is blue (risk averse)", "stop": "low of marubozu", "target": "nearest resistance"}

name: Bearish Marubozu
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Long red candle with no shadows (open = high, close = low); extreme selling; bearish regardless of prior trend.
conditions: {"identify": "close < open and abs(high - open) <= tol*high and abs(close - low) <= tol*high", "entry": "short near close (or next day close if red)", "stop": "high of marubozu"}

name: Spinning Top
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Small real body with roughly equal upper and lower shadows; colour irrelevant; indecision - bulls and bears both failed.
conditions: {"identify": "body small relative to range and upper_shadow ~= lower_shadow"}
bot_use: Treat as volatility-expansion/indecision flag; reduce size or scale out; not an entry signal alone.
facts: ["In a downtrend - either more selling or reversal (~50/50); test with half quantity, add if reversal confirms.", "In an uptrend - bulls pausing or fatigued; book profit on ~50% of holding.", "Calm before the storm - a move is coming, direction uncertain; reduce position size."]

name: Doji
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Open ~= close (no or wafer-thin body), shadows any length; indecision like spinning top; often appear in clusters.
conditions: {"identify": "abs(close - open) <= small_frac * (high - low)"}
facts: ["A doji following a recognisable pattern (e.g. after a bearish engulfing) amplifies the move - 'panic plus uncertainty'."]

name: Paper Umbrella
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Small body near top of range with long lower shadow >= 2x body; called Hammer after a downtrend, Hanging Man after an uptrend.
conditions: {"identify": "lower_shadow >= 2*body and upper_shadow small"}

name: Hammer
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Paper umbrella at the bottom of a downtrend; bulls rejected new lows; bullish reversal. Longer lower shadow = more bullish; blue body slightly preferred.
conditions: {"prior_trend": "downtrend", "identify": "lower_shadow >= 2*body and abs(close-open)/open within ~1-2% and close near high", "entry": "near close of hammer day (risk taker) or next day close if blue (risk averse)", "stop": "low of hammer"}
facts: ["Author trusts hammer more than hanging man."]

name: Hanging Man
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Paper umbrella at the top of an uptrend; bears entered intraday; bearish reversal (less reliable than hammer per author because price recovered).
conditions: {"prior_trend": "uptrend", "identify": "lower_shadow >= 2*body", "entry": "short near close (or next day close if red)", "stop": "high of candle"}

name: Shooting Star
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Inverted umbrella at top of uptrend - small body near low with upper shadow >= 2x body; bears pushed price back from new high; bearish. Red body slightly more reliable.
conditions: {"prior_trend": "uptrend", "identify": "upper_shadow >= 2*body and lower_shadow small and close ~= low", "entry": "short near close (or next day if red)", "stop": "high of shooting star"}

name: Bullish Engulfing
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Two-candle bottom reversal - P1 red, P2 blue whose real body engulfs P1's real body.
conditions: {"prior_trend": "downtrend", "identify": "P1.close < P1.open and P2.close > P2.open and P2.open <= P1.close and P2.close > P1.open", "entry": "close of P2 (preferred - multi-day pattern) or day after if blue", "stop": "min(P1.low, P2.low)"}
facts: ["Engulfing real bodies is sufficient; shadows need not be engulfed. Preferred over piercing pattern."]

name: Bearish Engulfing
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Two-candle top reversal - P1 blue, P2 red whose body engulfs P1's body.
conditions: {"prior_trend": "uptrend", "identify": "P1.close > P1.open and P2.close < P2.open and P2.open >= P1.close and P2.close < P1.open", "entry": "short at close of P2", "stop": "max(P1.high, P2.high)"}
facts: ["A doji after a bearish engulfing is a highly profitable setup per author."]

name: Piercing Pattern
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Like bullish engulfing but P2's blue body covers 50% to <100% of P1's red body.
conditions: {"prior_trend": "downtrend", "identify": "P1 red, P2 blue, 0.5*P1.body <= (P2.close - P1.close) < P1.body", "stop": "pattern low"}

name: Dark Cloud Cover
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Like bearish engulfing but P2's red body covers 50% to <100% of P1's blue body; trade setup same as bearish engulfing.
conditions: {"prior_trend": "uptrend", "identify": "P1 blue, P2 red, 0.5*P1.body <= (P1.close - P2.close) < P1.body", "stop": "pattern high"}

name: Bullish Harami
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Bottom reversal - long red P1 then small blue P2 contained within P1's body ('pregnant'); surprise strength unnerves bears.
conditions: {"prior_trend": "downtrend", "identify": "P1 long red; P2 blue; P2.open > P1.close; P2.close < P1.open", "entry": "close of P2 or next day if blue", "stop": "min(P1.low, P2.low)"}

name: Bearish Harami
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Top reversal - long blue P1 then small red P2 inside P1's body.
conditions: {"prior_trend": "uptrend", "identify": "P1 long blue; P2 red; P2.open < P1.close; P2.close > P1.open", "entry": "short at close of P2 or next day if red", "stop": "max(P1.high, P2.high)"}

name: Gap Up / Gap Down
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Gap up = open above prior close (buyer enthusiasm, bullish); gap down = open below prior close (bearish); no trades occur in the gap.
conditions: {"gap_up": "open > prev_close (strict: open > prev_high)", "gap_down": "open < prev_close"}

name: Morning Star (and Morning Doji Star)
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Three-candle bottom reversal - long red P1, gap-down doji/spinning top P2, gap-up blue P3 closing above P1's open.
conditions: {"prior_trend": "downtrend", "identify": "P1 red (long); P2 gaps down and is doji/spinning top; P3 gaps up, blue, P3.close > P1.open", "entry": "close of P3 for both risk types", "stop": "lowest low of P1..P3"}
facts: ["If P2 is a doji it is called a morning doji star."]

name: Evening Star (and Evening Doji Star)
type:LABEL: CandlestickPattern
summary: Three-candle top reversal - long blue P1, gap-up doji/spinning top P2, gap-down red P3 closing below P1's open.
conditions: {"prior_trend": "uptrend", "identify": "P1 blue; P2 gaps up, doji/spinning top; P3 gaps down, red, P3.close < P1.open", "entry": "short at close of P3", "stop": "highest high of P1..P3"}

name: Support and Resistance (S&R)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Price zones expected to attract maximum buying (support, below CMP) or selling (resistance, above CMP); used for targets, entries and stop placement.
conditions: {"level_valid": "count(swing pivots within +/-tol of level) >= 3 and pivots spaced in time", "is_support": "level < cmp", "is_resistance": "level > cmp"}
bot_use: Detect swing pivots, cluster by price with tolerance, keep clusters with >=3 well-spaced touches; use nearest opposite level as target and require stop near a level.
facts: ["Long trade target = nearest resistance; short trade target = nearest support.", "Construction: (1) load 3-6 months (short-term, for intraday/BTST) or 12-18 months (long-term, for swing) of data; (2) find price action zones - hesitation after up move, hesitation after down move, sharp reversals; (3) find >= 3 zones at the same price, well spaced in time (e.g. >= 2 weeks apart); (4) fit a horizontal line.", "More zones and wider time spacing = stronger level.", "Treat S&R as a zone (e.g. 429 +/- 3), not a point.", "Well-constructed S&R is usually respected but it is probabilistic.", "Accumulation creates support; distribution creates resistance (Dow)."]

name: Volume and the Volume-Price Trend Table
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Shares traded (one buy + one sell of 100 = volume 100); used to confirm trends; high volume implies institutional 'smart money'.
conditions: {"high_volume": "volume > SMA(volume, 10)", "low_volume": "volume < SMA(volume, 10)", "price_up_vol_up": "bullish", "price_up_vol_down": "caution - weak hands buying / possible bull trap", "price_down_vol_up": "bearish", "price_down_vol_down": "caution - weak hands selling / possible bear trap"}
bot_use: Volume filter for entries - require volume >= 10-day average on the signal bar.
facts: ["Volume figure in terminals is cumulative for the day. Avoid trading on low-volume days."]

name: Moving Averages (SMA / EMA)
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: Rolling average of closes; SMA weights equally, EMA weights recent data more and reacts faster (preferred). Lagging trend-following tool.
facts: ["Bullish when price > EMA; bearish when price < EMA.", "Works brilliantly in trends, whipsaws in sideways markets.", "Take all signals - many small losses, one big winner pays for them; can't pick the winner in advance."]

name: Price vs 50-day EMA System
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Long when close crosses above 50 EMA; exit when close crosses below.
conditions: {"entry_long": "close crosses above EMA(close, 50)", "exit_long": "close crosses below EMA(close, 50)"}
caveats: ["Many marginal/losing signals in sideways markets."]

name: Moving Average Crossover System
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Long when fast EMA crosses above slow EMA; exit when fast crosses below; fewer whipsaws than single MA.
conditions: {"entry_long": "EMA(fast) crosses above EMA(slow)", "exit_long": "EMA(fast) crosses below EMA(slow)"}
bot_use: Baseline trend-following strategy; combine with ADX/regime filter to avoid sideways whipsaw.
facts: ["Longer timeframe combos give fewer signals. 'The trend is your friend'."]

name: Leading vs Lagging Indicators; Oscillators; Momentum
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Leading indicators (mostly bounded oscillators like RSI) signal reversals in advance but give false signals; lagging indicators (MAs) confirm after the fact. Momentum = rate of price change.

name: Relative Strength Index (RSI)
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: J. Welles Wilder's 0-100 momentum oscillator of internal strength; strongest in sideways markets.
conditions: {"classical_long": "RSI < 30 (oversold)", "classical_short": "RSI > 70 (overbought)", "persistent_overbought": "RSI stuck > 70 for long -> look to BUY (excess positive momentum)", "persistent_oversold": "RSI stuck < 30 for long -> look to SELL", "exit_oversold": "RSI crosses back above 30 after prolonged oversold -> long", "exit_overbought": "RSI crosses back below 70 after prolonged overbought -> short"}
facts: ["Shorter lookback = more volatile RSI. Parameters are not sacred - develop your own edge. Rarely used standalone."]

name: MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence)
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: Gerald Appel's momentum/trend indicator - MACD line = 12 EMA - 26 EMA; signal line = 9-period EMA of MACD.
conditions: {"centerline_bull": "macd_line crosses above 0", "centerline_bear": "macd_line crosses below 0", "signal_bull": "macd_line crosses above signal_line", "signal_bear": "macd_line crosses below signal_line"}
facts: ["Sign = direction of momentum; magnitude = strength but scales with price level. Works in trends", "poor sideways."]

name: Bollinger Bands
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: John Bollinger's 20 SMA with +/-2 standard deviation bands; mean-reversion tool.
conditions: {"short": "price touches upper band -> target middle", "long": "price touches lower band -> target middle", "failure": "envelope expansion (bands widening as price rides a band) = trending market, signals fail"}
facts: ["Works in sideways markets", "fails in trends. Expect the trade to work almost immediately; if not", "suspect envelope expansion."]

name: Fibonacci Retracements
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: After a sharp move (trough to peak = 100%), price tends to retrace to 23.6%, 38.2% or 61.8% before resuming the trend.
facts: ["Use only as a confirmation tool; strong buy when stop coincides with Fib level plus pattern", "S&R and volume."]

name: Dow Theory
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Charles Dow's framework (compiled by Hamilton) - 9 tenets on trends, confirmation and market phases.
facts: ["Indices discount everything.", "Three trends - primary (1 to several years), secondary (counter-trend corrections, weeks to months), minor (daily noise).", "All indices must confirm each other (Nifty, midcap, smallcap move together).", "Volume must confirm - in uptrend volume rises on up moves, falls on dips; opposite in downtrend.", "Sideways markets can substitute for secondary trends.", "Close is the most sacred price.", "Before going long on a pattern, check primary trend; trading against a secondary counter-trend needs caution."]

name: Market Phases (Accumulation, Mark-up, Distribution, Mark-down)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Cycle - smart money accumulates after steep sell-off (creates support), mark-up is a fast rally that leaves public behind, distribution when public buys near highs (creates resistance), then mark-down sell-off.
facts: ["No two cycles are the same; can span months to years."]

name: Double / Triple Top and Bottom
type:LABEL: ChartPattern
summary: Reversal patterns where a price level is tested twice (or thrice) with tests well spaced in time (>= ~2 weeks); triple is stronger than double.
conditions: {"double_bottom": "two lows within tolerance, separated by >= ~10 sessions with a rebound between -> bullish", "double_top": "two highs within tolerance (e.g. 336 vs 332 accepted) -> bearish"}
facts: ["Best when the second test forms a candlestick pattern (e.g. shooting star on 2nd top)."]

name: Trading Range (Sideways Market)
type:LABEL: ChartPattern
summary: Price oscillates between fixed support and resistance for weeks to years; buy near the bottom, short near the top.
facts: ["Causes - no fundamental triggers, or waiting for a big announcement (short-lived).", "Longer range duration -> wider range."]

name: Range Breakout / Breakdown
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Breakout of a range often starts a new trend; true breakouts have high volume and high momentum; false breakouts have low volume and fall back into range.
conditions: {"entry_long": "close > range_high with volume > avg volume", "stop_long": "range_high (the broken resistance)", "entry_short": "close < range_low with high volume", "stop_short": "range_low", "min_target": "breakout_level +/- range_width"}

name: Flag Formation
type:LABEL: ChartPattern
summary: Steep rally (pole) then 5-15 session low-volume correction in a parallel channel; price then resumes sharply upward - second chance to buy.
conditions: {"identify": "sharp rally then 5-15 bar pullback within parallel lines on declining volume", "entry": "break above flag channel (act fast)"}
facts: ["Pullback is retail profit-taking; smart money stays invested."]

name: Reward-to-Risk Ratio (RRR)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Expected reward per unit of risk; trades below your RRR threshold must be dropped regardless of setup quality.

name: Grand 6-Point TA Checklist
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: (1) recognisable candlestick pattern; (2) stop near S&R (long - pattern low near support; short - pattern high near resistance); (3) volume >= 10-day average; (4) Dow Theory context (primary/secondary trend, double/triple/range/flag); (5) indicators (RSI/MACD) confirm -> scale size up, else proceed at reduced size; (6) RRR >= threshold (1.5 for active traders).
conditions: {"must_have": ["candlestick_pattern", "sr_near_stop", "volume_confirm", "rrr_ok"], "sr_distance_max": "abs(stop - sr_level)/stop <= 0.04 else skip", "indicator_rule": "if indicators confirm: size = full (e.g. 500); else size = reduced (e.g. 300)", "trade_quality": "satisfy at least 3-4 checklist points; prefer stock with more points over prettier pattern"}
bot_use: Encode as a scoring function; hard filters for 1,2,3,6 and size multiplier for 5.
facts: ["Discipline is ~80% of trading success; checklist enforces it.", "Engulfing preferred over piercing/dark cloud when checklist scores tie.", "Choosing not to trade is itself a big trading decision."]

name: Swing Trade Scanning Process
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Universe Nifty 50, EOD charts, 6-12 month look-back (2 yr for S&R); Part 1 shortlist charts with a pattern in last 3-4 candles; Part 2 evaluate 4-5 shortlisted charts against checklist; at most 1-2 qualify.
bot_use: Direct blueprint for an EOD scanner pipeline.
facts: ["Evaluation order: pattern strength -> prior trend -> volume >= 10-day avg -> S&R within 4% of stop -> Dow patterns & primary/secondary trend -> RRR >= 1.5 (target = S&R) -> MACD/RSI for sizing.", "Positional trades may be squared off intraday if target hits same day.", "Opportunity universe criteria - liquid (tight bid-ask, e.g. >= 5 lakh shares/day), EQ segment, not operator-driven; index stocks satisfy these."]

name: Opportunity Universe
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Fixed list of liquid stocks you scan daily (e.g. Nifty 50).
conditions: {"liquidity": "avg daily volume >= 500000 or tight bid-ask spread", "segment": "EQ"}

name: Scalping
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Large-size trades held minutes on 1m/5m charts for small moves; for seasoned traders.
facts: ["Use candlestick pattern + volume from checklist; RRR 0.5-0.75 acceptable.", "Only liquid stocks; quick to book losses; watch bid-ask and global markets (e.g. Hang Seng); low-cost broker essential; don't over-leverage; stop trading on bad days."]

name: ADX / +DI / -DI (Directional Movement)
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: Wilder's trend-strength system; ADX measures strength (not direction), +DI/-DI give direction.
conditions: {"strong_trend": "ADX > 25", "weak_trend": "ADX < 20", "buy": "ADX >= 25 and +DI crosses above -DI", "sell": "ADX >= 25 and -DI crosses above +DI", "stop": "low (long) / high (short) of signal candle; trade valid until stop breached"}
bot_use: Regime filter - enable trend systems when ADX > 25, mean-reversion when ADX < 20.

name: Alligator (Bill Williams)
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: Three displaced SMAs - jaw 13, teeth 8, lips 5.
conditions: {"buy": "close > SMA5 > SMA8 > SMA13 and lines separated", "sell": "close < SMA5 < SMA8 < SMA13 and lines separated", "no_trade": "lines intertwined/flat"}

name: Aroon and Aroon Oscillator
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: Tushar Chande's time-since-high/low indicator (0-100); default 25 (Kite 14).
conditions: {"buy": "aroon_up > 50 and aroon_down < 30", "sell": "aroon_down > 50 and aroon_up < 30", "strong_up": "oscillator > 50", "strong_down": "oscillator < -50"}

name: Average True Range (ATR)
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: Wilder's volatility measure including gaps; no direction; in price units.
formula: {"true_range": "max(high-low, abs(high-prev_close), abs(low-prev_close))", "atr": "Wilder smoothing / average of TR over n"}
conditions: {"expected_range": "price +/- ATR", "volatility_stop_long": "stop <= entry - ATR", "volatility_stop_short": "stop >= entry + ATR", "skip": "if ATR-based stop violates RRR, skip trade"}
bot_use: Volatility-normalised stops and position sizing.

name: ATR Bands
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: MA (default 5) +/- ATR envelope; price piercing a band suggests continuation in that direction; alternative to Bollinger.

name: Supertrend
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: ATR-based trailing trend line (Kite default period 7, multiplier 3); green below price in uptrends, red above in downtrends.
conditions: {"buy": "close crosses above supertrend (turns green)", "sell": "close crosses below supertrend (turns red)", "trail": "hold long until close below green line"}
facts: ["Fewer false signals than MA systems; works best in trending markets. Higher multiplier = fewer signals."]

name: VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price)
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: Intraday cumulative volume-weighted typical price; gauges intraday direction and execution quality.
conditions: {"intraday_bull": "price > VWAP", "intraday_bear": "price < VWAP", "good_long_fill": "buy price < VWAP", "good_short_fill": "short price > VWAP"}
caveats: ["Intraday only; ignore jump at 9:15 open; lags price."]

name: M03 - Fundamental Analysis
type:LABEL: Module
summary: Investor mindset, compounding, qualitative and quantitative investable-grade attributes, reading annual reports and the three financial statements, profitability/leverage/operating/valuation ratios, DuPont, index valuation, equity research process with 10-point checklist, DCF valuation, margin of safety, when to sell and portfolio size.

name: Fundamental Analysis (FA)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Holistic study of a business to identify investment-grade companies for long-term (3-5+ yr) wealth creation, separating business performance from short-term price noise.
facts: ["Wealth creators (Infosys, TCS, Page, Eicher, Bosch, Nestle, TTK Prestige) compounded >20% CAGR for 10+ years; wealth destroyers include Suzlon, Reliance Power, Sterling Biotech.", "At 20% CAGR money doubles in ~3.5 years (rule of 72).", "Skills needed - reading financial statements, understanding business in its industry, basic arithmetic.", "Tools - annual report, industry data, news, Excel.", "TA and FA should coexist (Eicher flat 2006-2010 then multi-bagger - short-term trades fill the gap)."]

name: Core-Satellite Capital Allocation
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Split capital (e.g. 60/40) - core in fundamentally strong long-term holdings (expect 12-15% CAGR), satellite for active TA trading in equity/F&O (expect 10-12% absolute/yr).
bot_use: Allocate a capped satellite bucket to algorithmic strategies while core remains long-term.

name: Speculator vs Trader vs Investor
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Speculator bets on blind faith/outside views; trader designs and backtests trades (e.g. selling high-IV options before RBI expecting volatility drop); investor ignores short-term noise and may buy more on overreaction.
facts: ["Doing nothing is itself a market action. A trader 'designs all his trades and not just speculates on an outcome'."]

name: Compounding Effect
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Reinvesting gains lets money grow on itself; the longer you stay invested, the faster absolute wealth grows.

name: Investable-Grade Attributes (Qualitative + Quantitative)
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Qualitative (weighted more by author) - management background, ethics, corporate governance, minority shareholder treatment, clandestine promoter share transactions, related-party transactions, promoter salaries, operator activity, significant shareholders, political affiliation, promoter lifestyle. Quantitative - profit/margin/earnings growth, expenses, efficiency, pricing power, taxes, dividends, cash flows, debt, working capital, assets, ratios.
facts: ["A red flag in any qualitative factor overrides great margins - the market eventually punishes poor governance.", "Sector-specific metrics matter (retail - stores, sales/sq ft; oil & gas - reserves, exploration costs).", "Hold as long as attributes remain intact; sell when they crumble (not because of price alone)."]

name: Annual Report
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Official yearly disclosure (data as of 31 March) - financial highlights, chairman's message, MD&A, 10-yr highlights, directors' report, corporate governance, financial statements, notice.
facts: ["Prefer AR over media websites (reclassification can distort).", "MD&A is the most important section - macro, industry, segment performance, outlook; compare with peers' ARs.", "Check chairman's realism (e.g. claims 10% growth when history is 4-5% = red flag).", "Standalone vs consolidated statements - prefer consolidated (includes subsidiaries).", "Line items reference notes/schedules with details."]

name: Profit & Loss Statement (Income Statement)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Revenue, expenses, tax and EPS for a period (year/quarter); top line = revenue, bottom line = PAT.
formula: {"net_revenue_from_ops": "sale of products (net of excise) + services + other operating revenue", "total_revenue": "revenue_from_operations + other_income", "pbt": "total_revenue - total_expenses - exceptional_items", "pat": "pbt - taxes", "eps": "pat / shares_outstanding"}
facts: ["Other income (interest, dividends, royalty) should be small; large other income is a red flag.", "Depreciation spreads tangible asset cost over useful life; amortisation for intangibles; P&L doesn't show the actual capex outflow (cash flow does).", "Exceptional items are one-off.", "Negative 'change in inventories' means more produced than sold."]

name: Balance Sheet
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Cumulative (flow-basis) statement of assets, liabilities and shareholders' equity; Assets = Liabilities + Equity.
formula: {"equation": "assets = shareholders_funds + non_current_liabilities + current_liabilities", "equity": "share_capital + reserves + surplus", "share_capital": "face_value * shares", "shares_outstanding": "share_capital / face_value", "net_block": "gross_block - accumulated_depreciation"}
facts: ["Shareholders' funds appear on liability side because the company owes them to shareholders.", "Reserves - capital, securities premium, general; surplus accumulates PAT, pays dividends.", "Non-current liabilities (>12 months) - long-term borrowings, deferred tax liability (depreciation timing), long-term provisions (employee benefits).", "Current liabilities - short-term borrowings (working capital), trade payables, other, short-term provisions.", "Non-current assets - tangible/intangible fixed assets, CWIP, investments, long-term loans/advances.", "Current assets - inventory, trade receivables, cash & equivalents, short-term loans/advances.", "No debt is good but ask why (can't borrow? not expanding?).", "P&L links - PAT -> surplus; credit sales -> receivables; purchases -> payables/inventory; capex -> depreciation; debt -> finance cost."]

name: Cash Flow Statement
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: True cash generated/consumed across operating, investing and financing activities; net cash flow ties to balance sheet cash.
facts: ["Revenue can include credit sales not yet collected - cash flow shows real liquidity.", "Liabilities up -> cash up; assets up -> cash down.", "Positive cash from operations is a sign of financial well-being; investors should focus on CFO.", "Healthy investing outflow signals expansion."]

name: Financial Ratios (overview)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Popularised by Benjamin Graham; categories - profitability, leverage, valuation, operating. A ratio alone is mute - compare with peers and its own trend; adjust for accounting policy changes; use averages of opening/closing balance sheet values.

name: EBITDA and EBITDA Margin
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Operating profitability excluding other income, finance cost and D&A; reflects management efficiency.

name: PAT Margin (Net Profit Margin)
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Overall profitability after all expenses and tax.

name: Return on Equity (RoE)
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Profit per unit of shareholders' equity; key investable attribute. Top Indian companies average 14-16%; author prefers >18-20% (checklist >25%) without high debt.
caveats: ["Debt inflates RoE (pizza oven example 25% -> 31% -> 50% as debt rises); always inspect with DuPont and debt levels."]

name: DuPont Model
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: RoE = Net profit margin x Asset turnover x Financial leverage; reveals quality of returns.

name: Return on Assets (RoA)
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Efficiency of asset use, adding back after-tax interest (tax shield) since lenders fund assets.

name: Return on Capital Employed (ROCE)
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Return on total capital (debt + equity).

name: Interest Coverage Ratio
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Ability to service interest from operating earnings; low coverage = default risk.

name: Debt to Equity Ratio
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Total (short + long-term) debt relative to equity; >1 indicates high leverage.
conditions: {"caution": "de > 1"}

name: Debt to Asset Ratio
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Share of assets financed by debt.

name: Financial Leverage Ratio
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Assets supported per unit of equity; higher = more leveraged.

name: Operating (Activity / Management) Ratios
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Efficiency of converting assets into revenue.
formula: {"fixed_asset_turnover": "operating_revenue / avg_net_fixed_assets_incl_cwip", "working_capital": "current_assets - current_liabilities", "working_capital_turnover": "revenue / avg_working_capital", "total_asset_turnover": "operating_revenue / avg_total_assets", "inventory_turnover": "COGS / avg_inventory", "inventory_days": "365 / inventory_turnover", "receivable_turnover": "revenue / avg_receivables", "dso": "365 / receivable_turnover", "cogs": "materials + stock-in-trade purchases + stores & spares + power & fuel"}
caveats: ["High inventory turnover could reflect low production capacity - investigate funding", "raw material access", "scalability."]

name: Asset Turnover
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Revenue generated per rupee of average total assets.

name: Gross Profit Margin
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: (Net sales - COGS)/Net sales; >20% suggests a moat.

name: Earnings Per Share (EPS)
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: PAT per outstanding share; EPS growth should track PAT growth (else dilution).

name: Price to Sales (P/S)
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Price relative to sales per share; useful when earnings are cyclical or distorted.
caveats: ["Higher-margin firms justify higher P/S - check profit margin."]

name: Price to Book Value (P/BV)
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Price relative to book (liquidation) value per share.

name: Price to Earnings (P/E)
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Price paid per rupee of earnings - the 'financial ratio superstar'.
facts: ["Author avoids buying stocks above 25-30x earnings regardless of sector.", "Earnings can be manipulated - watch frequent accounting policy changes, low depreciation provisions, earnings rising without cash flow and sales."]

name: Valuation Ratios
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Compare price with financial performance (P/S, P/BV, P/E); a mediocre business at a cheap valuation can beat an exciting one at a high valuation.

name: Nifty Index Valuation (P/E bands)
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Nifty P/E historically 16-20x (avg ~18x); peaked 28x (Jan 2008, pre-crash), troughed ~11x (late 2008/09).
conditions: {"caution": "nifty_pe >= 22", "attractive": "nifty_pe <= 16"}
bot_use: Macro valuation regime filter for long-only equity allocation / leverage.
caveats: ["Bands are from source era (2014); P/E methodology changed to consolidated earnings in 2021 - recalibrate."]
facts: ["NSE publishes daily Nifty P/E", "P/B", "dividend yield (~6 PM)."]

name: Stock Idea Generation
type:LABEL: Process
summary: General observation (Peter Lynch), stock screeners (e.g. ROE > 25% and PAT margin > 20%), macro trends, sectoral trends, special situations, circle of competence; maintain a watch list and re-evaluate.

name: Economic Moat
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Sustainable competitive advantage (brand, pricing power, licence, market share) protecting long-term profits (Buffett).

name: 3-Stage Equity Research
type:LABEL: Process
summary: (1) Understand the business via Q&A from 5 years of annual reports (~15 hrs, summarise on one page; stop on any red flag); (2) apply the checklist; (3) valuation via DCF and margin of safety. Stages are sequential.
facts: ["Key questions - what the company does, promoters' background, products, plants & capacity utilisation, raw material dependency (govt-regulated?), clients, competitors (monopoly/duopoly/oligopoly = higher margins), major shareholders, new products/geographies, revenue mix, regulation, bankers & auditors, labour issues, entry barriers, replicability in cheap-labour countries, number of subsidiaries.", "Author prefers businesses with little competition and little government intervention.", "Bear markets move prices, not fundamentals - conviction lets you buy in bear markets."]

name: 10-Point Fundamental Checklist
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Screen for investable-grade financials.
conditions: {"gross_profit_margin": "> 20%", "revenue_and_pat_growth": "in line with each other; author prefers revenue & PAT CAGR > 15%", "eps": "EPS growth consistent with net profit growth (no dilution)", "debt": "not highly leveraged; track Debt/EBIT trend and interest coverage", "inventory": "manufacturing - inventory growing with PAT; stable/declining inventory days", "sales_vs_receivables": "sales not driven by receivables (receivables % of sales stable/declining)", "cfo": "positive cash flow from operations", "roe": "> 25% (author elsewhere >20%), not debt-driven", "business_diversity": "1-2 simple business lines", "subsidiaries": "few (many subsidiaries can mean siphoning)"}
bot_use: Direct screener rules for a fundamental-filtered universe.

name: Time Value of Money (FV, PV, NPV)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Money's value changes over time due to opportunity cost; compounding moves money forward, discounting moves it back.
formula: {"fv": "amount * (1 + r) ** n", "pv": "amount / (1 + r) ** n", "npv": "sum(cf_t / (1 + r) ** t)"}

name: Free Cash Flow (FCF)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Operating cash after capex - cash available to shareholders; mark of a healthy business.

name: Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) Valuation
type:LABEL: Model
summary: Intrinsic value = PV of projected FCF + PV of terminal value, adjusted for net debt, divided by shares.
formula: {"base_fcf": "average FCF of last 3 years (smooths cyclicality)", "projection": "stage 1 (yrs 1-5) growth g1 (e.g. 18%, 15% for large caps), stage 2 (yrs 6-10) g2 (e.g. 10%)", "terminal_value": "FCF_10 * (1 + g_t) / (r - g_t)", "pv_terminal": "TV / (1 + r) ** 10", "equity_value": "sum PV(FCF) + PV(TV) - net_debt", "net_debt": "total_debt - cash", "intrinsic_value_per_share": "equity_value / shares", "value_band": "IV * [0.9, 1.1]"}
conditions: {"buy": "price < lower band", "hold": "lower band <= price <= upper band (no fresh buy)", "overvalued": "price > upper band (book profits or hold, never buy)"}
caveats: ["Garbage in, garbage out - requires forecasting.", "Highly sensitive to terminal growth (3.5% -> 4% moves value 368 -> 394).", "Needs constant updates; useless for <1 yr horizon.", "Keep assumptions conservative - FCF growth <= 20%, terminal growth <= 4%, 10-year 2-stage."]

name: Margin of Safety
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Benjamin Graham's principle - buy only at a discount to intrinsic value; author takes a further >= 30% discount to the lower value band.
facts: ["Bear markets offer such discounts - keep cash ready."]

name: When to Sell (Investing)
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Hold while investable-grade attributes stay intact; sell when they deteriorate, not because of price gains alone.

name: Number of Stocks in a Portfolio
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Author holds ~13, never >15; >20 is pointless. Klarman 10-15, Buffett 5-10, Graham 10-30, Keynes 2-3.

name: Investing Principles (Finale)
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Expect realistic 15-18% CAGR; long-term approach; buy investable-grade attributes; character over numbers; ignore TV noise and apply checklist; respect margin of safety; avoid IPOs (usually overpriced) unless 3-stage research; keep learning.
facts: ["Recommended books - Essays of Warren Buffett; Little Book that Beats the Market (Greenblatt); Little Book of Valuation (Damodaran); Little Book that Builds Wealth (Dorsey)."]

name: M04 - Futures Trading
type:LABEL: Module
summary: Forwards vs futures, futures trade mechanics, leverage and linear payoff, margins (SPAN + exposure) and daily M2M, margin calls, expiry/rollover, product types (NRML/MIS/CO/BO), trailing stops, shorting, Nifty futures and impact cost, futures pricing (spot-futures parity), cash & carry and calendar spreads, hedging with beta, open interest.

name: Derivatives
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Securities whose value is derived from an underlying (stock, index, bond, commodity, currency); earliest reference in Kautilya's Arthashastra (320 BC).

name: Forward Contract
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: OTC private agreement to exchange an asset at a fixed price on a future date; settled physically or in cash.
facts: ["Risks - liquidity (finding counterparty), default/counterparty, regulatory (unregulated), rigidity (cannot exit mid-way).", "Buyer profits if price rises above agreed price; seller profits if it falls; linear payoff."]

name: Futures Contract
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Exchange-traded, standardised, SEBI-regulated, transferable, time-bound, mostly cash-settled agreement whose price mimics the underlying.
bot_use: Express short-term directional views with leverage; trade shorts overnight; hedge portfolios.
facts: ["Lot size = minimum tradable quantity; multiples of lot only.", "Margin (a % of contract value) is blocked on entry for both buyer and seller.", "Can square off any time before expiry; squaring off transfers risk to a counterparty.", "P&L credited/debited the same day (M2M).", "Zero-sum game - money transfers, not created.", "Linear payoff instrument.", "Indian equity derivatives expired on the last Thursday of the month (per source; expiry days have since changed - verify).", "Unclosed positions are auto-settled at spot on expiry as futures and spot converge."]

name: Spot Market vs Futures Market
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Spot = regular cash market; futures price moves in tandem with spot. Spot delivery buying is unleveraged, no time pressure, but T+settlement; futures are leveraged and time-bound.

name: Leverage
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Controlling a large contract value with a small margin; double-edged - magnifies gains and losses.
bot_use: Cap effective leverage (e.g. <= 10x); compute margin-wipeout distance before entry.

name: Margins (Initial, SPAN, Exposure, Maintenance)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Initial margin = SPAN + exposure, blocked while position is open; SPAN (exchange minimum, volatility-driven) acts as maintenance margin; exposure ~4-5% of CV extra cushion.
caveats: ["Margin rules changed after 2020 SEBI peak-margin regime; intraday leverage limits differ now."]
facts: ["Margin varies daily with futures price and volatility (higher expected volatility -> higher SPAN).", "Hedged positions (spreads) get large margin benefit (e.g. Bharat Forge long Jan + short Feb needed ~7.2k vs ~75k).", "Index futures margin ~12-15%; single stocks can be 45-60% (source era)."]

name: Mark to Market (M2M)
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Daily settlement of futures P&L using previous close as reference; reference price resets to each day's close.
formula: {"daily_m2m": "(close_t - ref_price) * qty * direction, ref = entry on day 1 else close_{t-1}"}
facts: ["Sum of daily M2M = total P&L. M2M plus margins virtually eliminate counterparty default."]

name: Margin Call
type:LABEL: Event
summary: When cash balance after M2M falls below SPAN (maintenance) margin, broker demands funds or force-closes positions.
conditions: {"trigger": "cash_balance + m2m < span_margin"}
bot_use: Monitor margin utilisation intraday; reduce positions before forced liquidation.

name: Expiry, Contract Months and Rollover
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Three concurrent monthly contracts (current/near, mid, far); price usually near < mid < far; on expiry a new far month is listed. Rollover = closing near-month and opening next month near expiry.
facts: ["Directional view must play out before expiry.", "Near month is most liquid, hence rollover is common.", "Rollover data - rolling longs = bullish perception, rolling shorts = bearish (perception only)."]

name: F&O Product Types (NRML, MIS, CO, BO)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: More risk information to broker RMS -> lower margin. NRML = carry forward (full SPAN+exposure); MIS = intraday (lower); CO = intraday + mandatory stop (lower still); BO = intraday + stop + target + optional trailing (same margin as CO).
caveats: ["Bracket orders were later discontinued by many brokers; check availability."]
facts: ["MIS/CO/BO auto-squared off ~3:20 PM. RMS cares about risk not reward", "so target doesn't lower margin."]

name: Overnight Risk
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Risk of adverse news/moves while markets are closed (e.g. crude spikes overnight hitting BPCL longs); longer holding = more risk = more margin.

name: Trailing Stop Loss
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Move the stop in the trade's favour as price advances to lock in profit and ride momentum beyond the original target.
conditions: {"step_rule": "for every N points of favourable move, raise stop by N (example N=15)"}
bot_use: Implement fixed-step, ATR-based or Supertrend trailing stops.

name: Shorting - Spot vs Futures
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Spot shorts must be squared off intraday (else short delivery -> auction penalty up to ~20%); futures shorts can be carried overnight with same margin and M2M as longs; short stop is always above entry.

name: Nifty (Index) Futures
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Futures on the Nifty index; most liquid derivative in India.
bot_use: Preferred instrument for systematic index strategies and portfolio hedges.
facts: ["Benefits vs stock futures - diversified (no unsystematic risk), hard to manipulate, very liquid (impact cost ~0.0125%), lower margins (12-15% vs up to 45-60%), broad economic call, TA works better, lower volatility (~16-17% vs 30%+ for stocks).", "Lot size changes over time (25 in 2015; verify current)."]

name: Liquidity
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Ease of buying/selling without moving price; liquid instruments have tight spreads, low impact cost, attract institutions, and lower volatility.

name: Impact Cost
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Round-trip loss (buy at best ask, sell at best bid) as % of mid price; proxy for liquidity and market-order slippage.
conditions: {"avoid_market_orders": "impact_cost >> 0.0125%"}
bot_use: Slippage model in backtests; liquidity filter for universe.

name: Futures Pricing (Spot-Futures Parity)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Futures fair value = spot adjusted for risk-free carry minus dividends; basis (spread) = futures - spot; converges to zero at expiry.
facts: ["Market price differs slightly from fair value due to costs, taxes, margins, expected dividends; gap widens with days to expiry.", "Futures > spot = premium (contango); futures < spot = discount (backwardation, from short-term demand/supply imbalance)."]

name: Cash & Carry Arbitrage
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: When futures trade far above fair value, buy spot and sell futures to lock the spread; unwind near expiry as prices converge.
conditions: {"entry": "futures_market - fair_value >> costs", "legs": "long spot, short futures (equal quantity)", "exit": "just before expiry (sell spot, buy futures)"}

name: Calendar Spread (Futures)
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Buy one expiry and sell another of the same underlying when their spread deviates from fair value; sell the expensive, buy the cheap.
conditions: {"entry": "near-month trades far above fair value while mid-month near fair -> short near, long mid", "assumption": "mid month stays near fair value; near converges to spot at expiry"}
facts: ["Hedged", "so margins are much lower; not entirely risk-free (liquidity", "execution", "volatility)."]

name: Hedging
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Taking an offsetting position to insulate an existing position from adverse moves (like a fence around a garden).
facts: ["Why hedge rather than hold or sell - a 25% fall needs a 33.3% rise to recover; selling and re-buying requires timing, loses LTCG benefit and adds costs.", "Single stock hedge - short equal quantity of its futures; position becomes market-neutral.", "Stocks without futures or small positions - use beta-adjusted Nifty futures; positions smaller than one Nifty lot need options."]

name: Systematic vs Unsystematic Risk
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Unsystematic (company-specific - revenue/margin decline, leverage, misconduct) is diversifiable (~21 stocks enough); systematic (GDP, rates, inflation, fiscal deficit, geopolitics) is not diversifiable but can be hedged.

name: Diversification
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Spreading capital across stocks/sectors to reduce unsystematic risk; benefit flattens beyond ~20-21 stocks.

name: Beta
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Sensitivity of a stock's returns to market returns; market beta = 1; <1 low beta, >1 high beta, <0 inverse.

name: Portfolio Hedge with Nifty Futures
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Short beta-weighted value of Nifty futures to neutralise systematic risk of a long portfolio.
bot_use: Automated beta-hedging overlay for long equity books.
caveats: ["Fractional lots impossible - perfect hedge rarely possible."]

name: Open Interest (OI)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Number of outstanding (open) derivative contracts; rises when new positions are created, falls when positions are closed, unchanged on transfers. Continuous across days unlike volume.
conditions: {"long_buildup": "price up & OI up -> bullish", "short_buildup": "price down & OI up -> bearish", "short_covering": "price up & OI down -> shorts covering (bearish trend may end)", "long_unwinding": "price down & OI down -> longs exiting (bullish trend may end)", "caution": "abnormally high OI with rapid price move = euphoria/leverage; small trigger can cause panic"}
bot_use: Classify each bar as long buildup/short buildup/short covering/long unwinding as a positioning feature.
facts: ["Sum of signed positions is always zero (zero-sum).", "Higher OI = more liquid market.", "Volume-price for derivatives - price up & volume up = more longs; price down & volume up = more shorts; price up & volume down = short covering; price down & volume down = long unwinding."]

name: M05 - Options Theory for Professional Trading
type:LABEL: Module
summary: Call/put basics, jargon, buyer/seller payoffs, moneyness, Greeks (delta, gamma, theta, vega), volatility (historical/forecast/implied/realised, India VIX), normal distribution and range estimation, SD-based option writing, volatility-based stops, volatility smile & cone, Greek interactions, Black-Scholes calculator, put-call parity, strike selection by time, and case studies (event IV crush).

name: Options (overview)
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Right but not obligation for the buyer (who pays premium) to buy (call) or sell (put) the underlying at a strike on/before expiry; seller/writer has the obligation. ~80% of Indian derivatives volume (source era).
facts: ["Indian history - index futures Jun 2000, index options Jun 2001, stock options Jul 2001, stock futures Nov 2001; real liquidity from ~2006.", "Options are cash settled in India (stock options later moved to physical settlement - verify).", "Option seller has natural statistical edge - 2 of 3 scenarios (flat, adverse) favour seller.", "Most traders trade premium changes rather than hold to expiry; premiums can swing 100-350% intraday.", "Option sellers tend to hold to expiry to earn full premium."]

name: Option Jargon (strike, underlying, premium, expiry, exercise, settlement, option chain)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Strike = anchor price; underlying = spot; premium = price paid by buyer to writer (never fixed, driven by Greeks); expiry = last valid date (3 monthly series per source); exercise = claiming the right (European - only on expiry); option chain lists all strikes with LTP, bid/ask, OI, volume, IV.
facts: ["CE = European call", "PE = European put. All Indian options are European (American stock options were discontinued)."]

name: European vs American Options
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: European options exercise only at expiry based on expiry-day spot; American anytime before expiry (hence more expensive). All Indian options are European.

name: Call Option (long and short)
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Buyer bullish with limited risk (premium) and unlimited upside; seller expects price not to rise above strike, earns limited premium with unlimited risk and must post futures-like margin.
formula: {"intrinsic_value_expiry": "max(0, spot - strike)", "long_call_pnl": "max(0, spot - strike) - premium_paid", "short_call_pnl": "premium_received - max(0, spot - strike)", "breakeven": "strike + premium"}

name: Put Option (long and short)
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Buyer bearish - right to sell at strike; seller bullish/neutral, earns limited premium with large risk.
formula: {"intrinsic_value_expiry": "max(0, strike - spot)", "long_put_pnl": "max(0, strike - spot) - premium_paid", "short_put_pnl": "premium_received - max(0, strike - spot)", "breakeven": "strike - premium"}
facts: ["Whether to buy a call or sell a put when bullish depends on premium attractiveness (pricing/IV)."]

name: Four Option Positions Summary
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Bullish - buy call or sell put; bearish - buy put or sell call. Buyers - limited risk, unlimited reward; sellers - limited reward, unlimited risk ('eat like a chicken, shit like an elephant' - Taleb/Das).
facts: ["Buying to close a short (or selling to close a long) is a square-off, not a new long/short.", "P&L formulas apply when held to expiry; premiums move continuously before expiry."]

name: Moneyness (ITM / ATM / OTM)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: ITM has positive intrinsic value; ATM strike is nearest to spot; OTM has zero intrinsic value. Calls - strikes below ATM are ITM; puts - strikes above ATM are ITM. ITM premiums > OTM premiums.
conditions: {"call_itm": "strike < spot", "call_otm": "strike > spot", "put_itm": "strike > spot", "put_otm": "strike < spot", "atm": "argmin |strike - spot|"}
facts: ["Intrinsic value can never be negative (preserves limited-loss property)."]

name: Option Greeks
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Sensitivities of premium - delta (spot), gamma (change in delta), theta (time), vega (volatility); computed by Black-Scholes; interact with each other.

name: Delta
type:LABEL: Greek
summary: Change in premium per 1-point change in underlying; calls 0..1, puts -1..0; ATM ~0.5, ITM -> 1, OTM -> 0. First derivative of premium.
bot_use: Size option positions by net delta exposure; use delta as ITM probability for strike selection; hedge to delta-neutral.
facts: ["Delta changes with spot (moneyness changes).", "Delta stages - predevelopment (deep OTM ~0, big % but needs huge move), take-off & acceleration (OTM->ATM, max bang for buck), stabilisation (ITM->deep ITM, delta -> 1).", "Deep ITM option (delta 1) behaves like futures - can substitute with lower capital but watch liquidity.", "Deltas are additive across options of same underlying; futures delta = 1; two ATM options ~ one future (but not a true surrogate - other Greeks act).", "Short call = negative delta; short put = positive delta.", "Delta ~ probability of expiring ITM (0.1 delta -> ~10%).", "Delta-neutral positions (net delta 0, e.g. long ATM CE + long ATM PE) are insulated from direction but exposed to vol and time."]

name: Delta Neutral Position
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Combined options position with net delta ~0; unaffected by small directional moves, sensitive to volatility and time.

name: Gamma
type:LABEL: Greek
summary: Rate of change of delta per point of underlying (2nd derivative of premium); always positive for long options. Long options = long gamma; short options = short gamma.
bot_use: Risk limits should use gamma-adjusted (scenario) delta, not lot counts.
facts: ["Gamma peaks at ATM; low for deep ITM/OTM.", "Near expiry ATM gamma shoots up; ITM/OTM gamma -> 0.", "Short gamma makes positions grow against you - a 10-lot short ATM (delta 5) can become delta 8.5 after a 70-pt adverse move.", "Avoid shorting ATM/high-gamma options, especially near expiry; never short ATM/ITM hoping they expire worthless; OTM options are better short candidates if held to expiry."]

name: Theta (Time Decay)
type:LABEL: Greek
summary: Premium lost per day from passage of time, all else equal; options are depreciating assets. Long options = negative theta; short options = positive theta (friend of sellers).
facts: ["Time decay is slow early in the series and accelerates sharply near expiry.", "Selling early collects more time value but decays slowly; selling near expiry collects less but decays fast."]

name: Premium = Intrinsic Value + Time Value
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Premium splits into intrinsic value (exercise value now) and time value (compensation to writer for time risk).

name: Volatility (standard deviation of returns)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Volatility = risk = standard deviation of (log) returns, expressed as %; higher SD = wider expected range.

name: Standard Deviation and Variance
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Variance = mean of squared deviations from mean; SD = sqrt(variance); measures dispersion/consistency.

name: Normal Distribution and Price Ranges
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Daily returns are a random walk but approximately normally distributed; ~68% within 1 SD, 95% within 2 SD, 99.7% within 3 SD; outside 3 SD = black swan.
