formula: {"period_mean": "daily_mean * days", "period_sd": "daily_sd * sqrt(days)", "upper": "spot * exp(period_mean + k*period_sd)", "lower": "spot * exp(period_mean - k*period_sd)"}
bot_use: Expected-move bands for strike selection, stop placement and position risk.
caveats: ["Real returns have fat tails - black swans happen more often than normal implies."]

name: SD-Based OTM Option Writing (author's method)
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Compute 1-SD (or 2-SD) expected range to expiry and sell options outside it; author sells only calls, ~1 SD away, on the Friday before expiry week.
conditions: {"range": "spot*(1 +/- (daily_mean*days +/- daily_sd*sqrt(days)))", "sell_calls": "strikes above upper 1SD bound", "sell_puts": "strikes below lower bound (author avoids puts - panic spreads faster than greed)", "timing": "last Friday before expiry week (~4-7 days to expiry); never > 15 days to expiry; use 2SD if writing earlier", "avoid": "events - monetary policy, results, policy decisions", "exit": "when written option turns ATM, or sentiment turns", "instruments": "Nifty, Bank Nifty, SBI, Infosys, Reliance, Tata Steel, Tata Motors, TCS (liquid only)"}
bot_use: Weekly premium-selling bot with SD strike selection, event calendar filter and ATM-touch exit.
caveats: ["Small steady gains", "rare catastrophic losses; keep costs minimal; paper-trade several expiries first."]

name: Author's Capital Allocation
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: 100% equity-oriented - 35% equity mutual funds via SIP (4 funds), 40% direct portfolio (~12 stocks, 5+ yrs), 25% short-term trading; max 35% of trading bucket per strategy (~9% of total capital).

name: Volatility-Based Stop Loss
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Place stop outside expected noise - entry minus (daily vol x sqrt(holding days)) - instead of a fixed %; re-check RRR with the new stop.
bot_use: Default stop model for swing strategies.

name: Volatility Types - Historical, Forecast, Implied, Realised; India VIX
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Historical (from past prices), forecast (models such as GARCH(1,1)), implied (market consensus embedded in premium - most valued), realised (actual over the period). India VIX = NSE's 30-day implied vol of Nifty options ('fear index').
bot_use: Regime filter (VIX level/percentile) for buying vs selling options; IV rank for strategy choice.
facts: ["Many professionals trade volatility rather than direction.", "VIX rises in steep/panic markets.", "Aug 24 2015 - Nifty -4.9%, VIX +64%, far OTM calls rose 50-80% (low delta + vega)."]

name: Vega
type:LABEL: Greek
summary: Change in premium per 1% change in volatility; positive for long calls and puts; impact largest with more time to expiry and for OTM options.
facts: ["30 days to expiry, vol 15->30% moved premium ~95%; 15 days ~50%; 5 days ~47%.", "Buy options when vol is expected to rise; sell when expected to fall.", "High IV raises cost and lowers profit potential of debit spreads (bull call spread 72 cost at 20% IV vs 82 at 35%)."]

name: Volatility Smile
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: IV is lowest at ATM and rises for strikes further OTM/ITM, plotting a smile.

name: Volatility Cone
type:LABEL: Model
summary: Plot min/-2SD/-1SD/mean/+1SD/+2SD/max of historical realised vol for different windows to expiry (10..90 days); overlay current IVs to spot rich (near +2SD -> short) or cheap (near -2SD -> buy) options.
conditions: {"short_vol": "current IV >= +2SD of realised vol for same days-to-expiry", "long_vol": "current IV <= -2SD"}
bot_use: Relative-value IV signal across strikes and underlyings.
caveats: ["Use only for liquid options."]

name: Greek Interactions
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Gamma vs time - ATM gamma explodes near expiry, ITM/OTM gamma -> 0; delta vs IV - high IV keeps far OTM deltas non-zero (explains rich far-OTM premiums), low IV flattens deltas at extremes.

name: Black-Scholes Option Pricing
type:LABEL: Model
summary: Inputs - spot (or futures for futures-based options), strike, risk-free rate (RBI 91-day T-bill), implied volatility, dividend (if ex-date before expiry), calendar days to expiry; outputs theoretical call/put prices and Greeks.
formula: {"d1": "(ln(S/K) + (r - q + sigma^2/2) T) / (sigma sqrt(T))", "d2": "d1 - sigma sqrt(T)", "call": "S e^{-qT} N(d1) - K e^{-rT} N(d2)", "put": "K e^{-rT} N(-d2) - S e^{-qT} N(-d1)"}
facts: ["Black & Scholes (1973)", "Merton; Nobel 1997. Small model errors expected."]

name: Put-Call Parity
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: For European options of same strike/expiry - put + spot = PV(strike) + call; at expiry put + spot = strike + call.
bot_use: Detect mispricing / synthetic positions (synthetic long = long call + short put).

name: Strike Selection by Series Half and Target Time
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Which strike to buy depends on when in the series you trade and how fast the target is expected.
conditions: {"first_half_target_5d": "far OTM (2 strikes from ATM)", "first_half_target_15d": "ATM or slightly OTM (1 strike)", "first_half_target_25d": "slightly ITM", "first_half_target_expiry": "ITM", "second_half_same_day": "far OTM (2-3 strikes)", "second_half_target_5d": "slightly OTM (1 strike)", "second_half_target_10d_or_expiry": "ATM or slightly ITM", "general": "buy options when vol expected to rise; sell when expected to fall; don't buy far OTM just because cheap - needs a fast move"}
bot_use: Map signal horizon & days-to-expiry to strike offset automatically.

name: Event Volatility Play (short straddle before event, exit before announcement)
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: IV rises into scheduled events (RBI policy, results); short ATM call + put a few days before and buy back as IV drops - ideally minutes before/at the announcement. Long straddles into events often lose because the losing leg's premium collapses faster than the winning leg gains.
conditions: {"entry": "2-4 days before known event, IV elevated, short ATM CE + ATM PE (liquid)", "exit": "time-based stop - just before announcement (or right after, as IV collapses)", "stop": "volatility-based, not premium-based"}
bot_use: Event-calendar driven vol-selling strategy with time exits.

name: Options Trading Lessons from Case Studies
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Prefer near-ATM strikes in stock options for liquidity; on 'exhaustion' views prefer selling calls (sideways likely) in 2nd half of series with SD-based strikes; author buys naked calls mainly on flag patterns (prior rally 5-10%, low-volume ~3% pullback); define entry, exit and stop for every trade.

name: M06 - Option Strategies
type:LABEL: Module
summary: Behavioural warning on gambling with options; bull call/put spreads, call ratio back spread, bear call ladder, synthetic long and put-call-parity arbitrage, bear put/call spreads, put ratio back spread, long/short straddle and strangle, max pain and PCR. (The source lists further strategies - straps, strips, iron condor, butterfly, box, synthetic put, bull put ladder - but does not cover them.)

name: Option Strategy Principles
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Know a handful of strategies well and map market view to strategy; never treat options as lottery tickets ('limited risk, unlimited profit' is a silent P&L killer); professionals prefer spreads for risk visibility even at lower profit; prefer net-credit strategies; always sum deltas to know a multi-leg position's directional bias.
facts: ["Moderate move quantified by volatility - volatile stocks 5-8%, less volatile stocks and indices < 5%.", "Delta-neutral strategies react to volatility and time ('volatility based strategies').", "Winning on options can be addictive (reflexive vs reflective brain)."]

name: View -> Option Strategy Map
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Map outlook and volatility view to a strategy.

name: Bull Call Spread (debit)
type:LABEL: Strategy

conditions: {"strike_first_half": "target in 5d -> far OTM pair; 15d -> slightly OTM; 25d/expiry -> ATM", "strike_second_half": "1-5d -> far OTM; 10d -> slightly OTM; expiry -> ATM"}

name: Bull Put Spread (credit)
type:LABEL: Strategy

name: Call Ratio Back Spread
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Outright bullish - sell 1 ITM call, buy 2 OTM calls (strict 2:1), usually for net credit; unlimited upside, small profit if market falls, max loss at higher strike.
conditions: {"strikes": "slightly ITM short + slightly OTM long when time is ample; in 2nd half use deep ITM short + slightly ITM long", "volatility": "rising IV helps with ample time; hurts with few days left; avoid starting when IV > ~2x normal"}

name: Bear Call Ladder (actually bullish)
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Sell 1 ITM call, buy 1 ATM and 1 OTM call (1:1:1) for net credit; profits big above upper breakeven, modest if market falls, loses if market stalls; best on stocks around quarterly results.

name: Synthetic Long (and PCP Arbitrage)
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Long ATM call + short ATM put replicates long futures (linear payoff); breakeven = strike + net premium. Arbitrage - synthetic long + short futures should net zero at expiry; a positive locked P&L after costs is an arbitrage.

name: Arbitrage
type:LABEL: Concept

name: Long / Short Straddle
type:LABEL: Strategy

name: Income Tax Basics (FY, AY, slabs)

name: Classifying Market Income (Investor vs Trader)
type:LABEL: Tax

name: Securities Transaction Tax (STT)
type:LABEL: Tax

name: Taxation of Trading as Business Income
type:LABEL: Tax

name: Loss Set-off and Carry-forward Rules
type:LABEL: Tax
summary: Must file on time to carry forward. Non-speculative (F&O) loss - same year vs any income except salary; carried forward 8 years vs non-speculative business income only. Speculative (intraday) loss - only vs speculative gains, carried 4 years. STCL - vs capital gains, 8 years.
conditions: {"speculative_loss_vs_fno_gain": "NOT allowed", "fno_loss_vs_speculative_gain": "allowed (same year)"}

type:LABEL: Strategy

name: BTST Tax Treatment
type:LABEL: Tax

name: Advance Tax
type:LABEL: Tax
summary: Business income or realised STCG requires advance tax instalments - 30% by 15 Sep, 60% by 15 Dec, 100% by 15 Mar (source; a 15 June instalment now also exists); ~12% p.a. interest on shortfall; pay on profits realised to date, claim refund if overpaid.

name: Business Turnover and Tax Audit (44AB / 44AD)
type:LABEL: Tax
summary: Audit if trading business turnover > Rs 1 Cr, or (44AD) turnover < 1 Cr but profit < 8% of turnover (unless total income below taxable limit). Trading turnover is not contract value.

name: Risk Management (overview)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Successful trading is ~80% money management, 20% strategy (Mark Douglas). Risk differs for single positions, multiple positions and portfolios; diversify to reduce unsystematic risk, hedge to reduce systematic risk; no position is ever 'safe'.

name: Expected Portfolio Return
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Weighted sum of asset expected returns; a probabilistic expectation, not a guarantee. Annualise daily mean x 252.

name: Variance, Covariance and Correlation Matrices
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Variance = dispersion of an asset's returns; covariance = co-movement sign of two assets; correlation = covariance / (sd_x sd_y). For k assets build the k x k variance-covariance matrix from the n x k excess-return matrix X, then the correlation matrix.
formula: {"variance": "sum((x - mean)^2)/N", "covariance": "sum((r1 - mean1)(r2 - mean2)) / (n - 1)", "cov_matrix": "(1/n) * X^T X, X = returns - column means", "corr_matrix": "cov_matrix / (sd sd^T)"}
facts: ["Diagonal of covariance matrix = variances; correlation matrix diagonal = 1, symmetric.", "Portfolio managers prefer low/negative covariance between holdings so they counterbalance."]

name: Portfolio Variance (Risk)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Portfolio volatility from weights, individual SDs and the correlation matrix; equivalently the SD of the portfolio's own daily returns (equity curve) - both give the same number.
formula: {"weighted_sd": "w_i * sd_i", "portfolio_sd": "sqrt( wsd^T * Corr * wsd )", "annualised": "daily_portfolio_sd * sqrt(252)", "range_1sd": "E[R] +/- sd_annual (68%), 2sd 95%, 3sd 99.7%"}
caveats: ["Short look-back in a bull market biases expected returns upward; use >= 1 year of data."]

name: Equity Curve
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Portfolio value normalised to Rs 100 over time (each holding compounding its daily returns at its weight); visualises performance, benchmark against Nifty; SD of its daily returns = portfolio volatility.
bot_use: Core performance artefact for any strategy/portfolio; derive drawdown, volatility, Sharpe.

name: Portfolio Optimisation and Efficient Frontier
type:LABEL: Model
summary: Varying weights changes risk and return. Solve (e.g. Excel Solver) for minimum-variance portfolio (min sd s.t. sum w = 1), and for each fixed risk level the max- and min-return portfolios; the upper envelope from the min-variance point is the efficient frontier - always choose portfolios on it.
formula: {"min_variance": "min_w sqrt(w^T Sigma w) s.t. sum(w) = 1", "max_return_at_risk": "max_w w^T mu s.t. sum(w)=1, sqrt(w^T Sigma w) = target"}
bot_use: Allocate across strategies/assets on the efficient frontier given a risk budget.
caveats: ["Add no-short (w >= 0) constraints for long-only; optimisation is sensitive to estimated returns."]

name: Value at Risk (VaR) and CVaR (historical)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Worst expected daily loss at a confidence level; historical method - check returns look normal (histogram), sort returns, VaR = worst value within best 95% of observations, CVaR = average of the worst 5%.
formula: {"var_95": "5th percentile of daily portfolio returns", "cvar_95": "mean(returns <= var_95)"}
bot_use: Daily risk report and pre-trade risk limit (portfolio VaR <= budget).
facts: ["Born after Black Monday (19 Oct 1987", "Dow -22.6%); JP Morgan's 4:15 PM report -> RiskMetrics."]

name: Gambler's Fallacy
type:LABEL: Psychology
summary: Believing a streak must end - increasing size after losses ('next one will win') or cutting size after wins; each independent trade has the same odds. Antidote - systematic position sizing.

name: Recovery Trauma (drawdown recovery math)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Gains needed to recover a loss grow non-linearly - small accounts that take big bets suffer most. Stay in the game ('if you lose all your chips you can't bet' - Larry Hite).
bot_use: Hard max-drawdown circuit breakers; reduce size during drawdowns.

name: Equity Estimation Models (Van Tharp)
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Core equity - subtract capital allocated to open trades (conservative); total equity - cash + margins blocked + open P&L (risky, counts unrealised); reduced total equity (author's preference) - core equity plus only locked-in profits (via trailing stops).

name: Position Sizing Techniques
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Decide how much capital/risk each trade gets. Methods - unit per fixed amount (e.g. 1 lot per 1L - simple, ignores risk, doesn't scale); percentage margin (fixed % of equity as margin per trade); percentage volatility (cap ATR-based volatility per position, e.g. 2% of equity); percentage risk (cap loss-at-stop at 1-3% of equity). Combine one equity model with one or two sizing methods.
formula: {"pct_volatility_shares": "(equity * vol_pct) / ATR", "pct_risk_qty": "(equity * risk_pct) / (abs(entry - stop) * lot_size)  [lots]", "classic_5pct_rule": "max exposure per trade = 5% of capital"}
bot_use: Mandatory sizing layer between signal and order - default to % risk with ATR/volatility stops, reduced-total-equity accounting.
facts: ["Professional traders rarely risk > 1-3% per trade.", "Think about total portfolio volatility exposure (e.g. 15% of capital on a bad day - does it churn your stomach?)."]

name: Kelly Criterion (and capped Kelly)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Optimal bet fraction from win rate and win/loss ratio; author scales a capped risk budget by Kelly% rather than betting full Kelly.
formula: {"kelly_pct": "W - (1 - W)/R", "W": "winning trades / total trades", "R": "average win / average loss", "capped": "risk_this_trade = kelly_pct * max_risk_pct (e.g. 5%)"}
bot_use: Scale per-trade risk by rolling backtest/live Kelly, capped.
caveats: ["Full Kelly is too aggressive - a 70% Kelly still leaves a large chance of a huge loss; estimates of W and R are noisy."]

name: Trading and Investing Biases
type:LABEL: Psychology
summary: Biases are what stand between you and a profitable P&L. Forgotten investments (MRF shares held 25 yrs -> Rs 128 Cr) show how attention + bias leads to early selling.

name: Illusion of Control
type:LABEL: Psychology
summary: Cluttering charts with many indicators creates false certainty; no analysis controls outcomes. Keep analysis simple and focus on statistics/odds.

name: Recency Bias
type:LABEL: Psychology
summary: Over-weighting the latest data (a green candle after a governance scandal) over the bigger picture; exit governance-tainted stocks regardless.

name: Anchoring Bias (Focalism)
type:LABEL: Psychology
summary: Fixating on the first price seen (author refused to pay 280-310 for Sundaram Clayton anchored at 270 and missed a multi-bagger); be willing to pay a small premium when thesis is intact.

name: Functional Fixedness
type:LABEL: Psychology
summary: Using tools only in conventional ways - e.g. treating NRML margin as locked; converting an overnight NRML position to MIS intraday frees margin for another intraday trade, then convert back before close.

name: Confirmation Bias
type:LABEL: Psychology
summary: Seeking only information that supports your view (reading routine news as a trigger for your chart thesis); counter with critical 'so what?' questioning.

name: Attribution Bias
type:LABEL: Psychology
summary: Crediting wins to skill and blaming losses on brokers/systems; counter by keeping a trading journal with entry and exit reasons.

name: Trading Journal
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Record why each trade was entered and exited to learn from your own behaviour and overcome attribution bias.
bot_use: Log every signal, filter decision, order, fill and exit reason for post-trade analysis.

name: M10 - Trading Systems
type:LABEL: Module
summary: What a trading system is (quantified, backtestable process vs ad-hoc views), pair trading via ratio/spread/differential with z-score/density curve (Mark Whistler method), statistical arbitrage via linear regression, error ratio, cointegration/stationarity/ADF test and residual z-score trading with beta-neutral sizing and intercept caution, statistical futures calendar spreads, and cross-sectional momentum portfolios. (Volatility-based delta hedging was announced but not covered.)

name: Trading System
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: A defined, quantified, backtestable process that takes market inputs, applies fixed logic and outputs a trade decision; gut, tips, TV, broker calls and ad-hoc 'systematic deduction' are not systems. Not a holy grail - you design the logic once and follow it; backtesting is mandatory and must be redone as markets change.

name: Backtesting
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Running a system's rules over historical data to measure frequency, win rate and P&L profile before risking capital; use clean, corporate-action-adjusted, date-aligned data; backtest per instrument and per direction (e.g. SBIN calendar spreads - shorts worked, longs mixed).
bot_use: Every node with 'conditions' should be backtested with realistic costs/slippage before deployment.

name: Pair Trading (Relative Value / Statistical Arbitrage) - concept
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Two similar businesses (e.g. HDFC Bank & ICICI Bank) share drivers so their prices move together; a stock-specific 'local event' causes a temporary anomaly - buy the relatively cheap, sell the relatively expensive and profit when the relationship normalises.
facts: ["Origin - Gerry Bamberger / Nunzio Tartaglia at Morgan Stanley (1980s); DE Shaw adopted it.", "Not truly market-neutral (two different underlyings); a calendar spread is closer to market-neutral.", "Relationship measures - spread (difference of % changes), differential (price difference), ratio (price1/price2); divergence vs convergence trades.", "Qualify pairs with correlation (Whistler method wants > 0.75; compute on returns).", "Margin-hungry; expect 2-3 signals per pair per year - track many pairs.", "Main risk - the pair keeps diverging (relationship breaks)."]

name: Mean Reversion
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: A stationary series (pair ratio, residual, spread) that deviates from its mean tends to return to it; probability of reversion inferred from its standard-deviation distance.

name: Pair Trading Method 1 - Ratio z-score / Density Curve (Mark Whistler)
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Track ratio = price_A / price_B; compute mean, SD (and SD table up to +/-3), and the cumulative normal 'density curve' value NORM.DIST(ratio, mean, sd, TRUE) daily; trade extremes, exit toward mean.
conditions: {"long_pair": "density in ~[0.003, 0.025] (ratio at -2..-3 SD) -> buy A (numerator), sell B", "short_pair": "density in ~[0.975, 0.997] (+2..+3 SD) -> sell A, buy B", "exit": "ratio back inside 2 SD / toward mean (e.g. density ~0.16-0.84)", "density_map": "0.16=-1SD, 0.84=+1SD, 0.025=-2SD, 0.975=+2SD, 0.003=-3SD, 0.997=+3SD"}
caveats: ["Correlation of Axis-ICICI only ~0.5 in example; author considers this method a foundation - prefers regression method; consider rupee neutrality."]

name: Linear Regression (for pairs)
type:LABEL: Model
summary: Fit y = M*x + c (+ residual) between two price series; outputs slope (beta/hedge ratio), intercept, residuals, standard error (SD of residuals) and standard error of intercept.

name: Error Ratio (choose X vs Y)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Regress both ways; pick the orientation with the lower error ratio (keeps intercept - the unhedged part - small).

name: Stationarity, Cointegration and the ADF Test
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Two prices are cointegrated if the regression residuals are stationary (constant mean, constant SD, no autocorrelation); test with Augmented Dickey-Fuller - p-value is probability of NON-stationarity; require p <= 0.05. Regression relations on non-stationary residuals are spurious.
conditions: {"tradable_pair": "adf_pvalue(residuals) <= 0.05", "manual_checks": "means of 3 sub-samples similar; SDs similar; lag-1/lag-2 autocorrelation ~0"}
bot_use: Weekly/biweekly re-screen of sector pairs (200-day lookback) with statsmodels.adfuller.

name: Pair Trading Method 2 - Regression Residual z-score (Stat Arb)
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: For same-sector pairs over 200 days - regress both ways, keep lower error ratio orientation, require ADF p <= 0.05, then trade the residual's z-score with beta-neutral quantities.
formula: {"z": "today_residual / SE_of_residuals", "qty_x": "qty_y * beta (round to lot sizes; top up in cash market if needed)", "unexplained_share": "intercept / price_y"}
conditions: {"long_pair": "z <= -2.5 (book: -2) -> buy Y, sell beta*X", "short_pair": "z >= +2.5 -> sell Y, buy beta*X", "stop_loss": "z beyond -3 (long) / +3 (short)", "target": "z back to -1 (long) / +1 (short), ideally mean", "skip": "negative beta (often untradeable); large intercept relative to price_y (e.g. 1626/2024 = 80% unexplained)"}
bot_use: Complete stat-arb pipeline - nightly screen, z-score monitor intraday, beta-neutral sizing, z-based exits.
facts: ["Price, S&R, RSI are irrelevant - only the residual z-score matters.", "Positions may stay open 7-25 sessions; keep M2M buffer.", "Beyond pairs - multivariate regression (stock A vs basket B+C)."]

name: Statistical Futures Calendar Spread
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Treat the next-month minus current-month futures price difference as a mean-reverting series (prices already embed carry, dividends etc.); trade +/-1 SD deviations back to the mean.
conditions: {"sell_spread": "spread > mean + 1sd -> sell next month, buy current month", "buy_spread": "spread < mean - 1sd -> buy next month, sell current month", "exit": "spread returns to mean"}
facts: ["Signals cluster near expiry; small P&L so costs must be minimal; directional risk removed so leverage can be higher; backtest per contract and per side."]

name: Momentum
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Rate of change of returns (use % not rupee changes); can be measured over any horizon (minutes for HFT to 12 months); consistency of returns matters.

name: Cross-Sectional Momentum Portfolio
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: From a tracking universe (e.g. BSE 500, or custom filters like mcap >= 1000 Cr; 150-200 stocks for a 12-15 stock portfolio), rank by trailing 12-month return, buy top 10-15 equally weighted on the first trading day of the month, rebalance monthly (sell drop-outs, buy new entrants).
conditions: {"universe": "liquid, clean, corporate-action adjusted", "entry": "top N by 12m return, equal weight", "rebalance": "monthly after close on last trading day", "variations": "1m/2w/1w lookbacks; skewed weights; fundamental momentum (quarterly sales growth, EPS growth, margins) rebalanced quarterly"}
bot_use: Monthly rebalancing bot with index-trend regime filter (e.g. Nifty above 200-DMA).
caveats: ["Works in up-trending markets; poor in choppy markets; bleeds more than the market in downtrends (author profited 2009-10", "hit in 2011) - add a market regime filter; backtest first."]

name: Event Overreaction Short Strangle (example of 'systematic deduction')
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Oct 2017 PSU recapitalisation - PSU bank index +27%, but Bank Nifty +3% looked excessive given PSU weight ~10%, so authors sold a Bank Nifty short strangle to capture falling IV (worked); illustrates contrarian reasoning that is not yet a system.

name: M11 - Personal Finance
type:LABEL: Module
summary: Start saving early, interest/compounding/TVM math, retirement corpus planning with inflation and step-up SIPs, mutual fund structure/NAV/factsheet, equity and debt fund categories, bonds/YTM, index funds vs active, arbitrage funds, return measurement (absolute/CAGR/XIRR/rolling), expense ratio and direct vs regular, benchmarking/TRI, risk metrics (beta, alpha, SD, Sharpe, Sortino, capture ratios), fund analysis, MF portfolio construction, smart beta, asset allocation & sequence risk, ETFs, and macroeconomics (GDP, fiscal deficit).

name: Start Saving Early (time > amount)
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Time in the market dominates amount invested - the triplet sisters example at 12% shows 4.5L invested age 20-28 grows to 4.89 Cr by 65, beating 19L invested age 28-65 (3.05 Cr).

name: Simple vs Compound Interest
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Simple interest only on principal; compound interest on principal plus accumulated interest.

name: Discount Rate = Risk-free + Risk Premium
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Opportunity cost used for PV/FV decisions = risk-free (government bond of matching tenor) + risk premium (~1.5-2%). Money today is worth more than money tomorrow.

name: Retirement Corpus Planning
type:LABEL: Model
summary: Inflate today's annual expense for each retirement year (FV at inflation ~5%) and sum to get the corpus; build it via monthly SIPs into equity funds with annual step-ups, each instalment compounding for its remaining months.
formula: {"expense_in_year_k": "annual_expense * (1 + inflation) ** years_from_now", "corpus": "sum over retirement years", "sip_fv": "sum_m installment_m * (1 + r) ** (months_remaining_m / 12)", "multi_asset_return": "sum(weight_i * expected_return_i)"}

name: Mutual Funds (structure, NAV, factsheet)
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Pooled vehicle - sponsor (promoter, holds licence) appoints trustee and AMC (investment manager); custodian holds assets; RTA services investors. Units issued at notional value; NAV moves with holdings. Factsheet - objective, open/close-ended, plans (direct vs regular), options (dividend/growth), riskometer.

name: SEBI Equity Fund Categories
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Market-cap classes - large cap = top 100 by full market cap, mid cap = 101-250, small cap = 251+. Large-cap funds >= 80% large caps; large & mid >= 35% each; also multi-cap, focused (max 30 stocks), dividend yield, ELSS (tax-saving, 3-yr lock-in), sectoral/thematic.
bot_use: Universe definitions for large/mid/small-cap strategies (rank by full market cap).

name: Market Capitalisation
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Share price x shares outstanding; market cap of the whole market tends to grow with GDP.

name: Debt Funds and Debt Risks
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Companies borrow via bonds (>1 yr) and commercial paper (<1 yr), government via T-bills/G-secs; lenders face credit, interest-rate, liquidity and rating-change risk. Overnight (1-day, tri-party repo) < liquid (<=91 days) < ultra-short (3-6 m Macaulay) < low duration < short/medium duration; banking & PSU (lower credit risk); credit risk funds (avoid as retail); gilts (no credit risk, high rate risk).
facts: ["Bond prices move inversely to yields/interest rates; modified duration ~ % NAV change per 1% rate change.", "Liquid funds are not savings accounts (Taurus, Franklin Templeton 2020 wind-up, DHFL defaults).", "Watch fund borrowing (liquidity stress), concentrated corporate exposure, sub-investment-grade paper; hold at least the fund's average maturity."]

name: Bonds and Yield to Maturity
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Coupon is % of face value; YTM is the effective yield given purchase price, coupons and maturity; buyer pays accrued interest to seller; tax-free bonds have tax-free coupons; PSU bonds carry implicit sovereign backing.

name: Index Funds (passive investing)
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Track a benchmark cheaply; active management is a zero-sum game before costs and negative after costs - SPIVA India - ~82% of large-cap funds underperformed BSE 100 over 5 yrs (2019); expense gap ~1% compounds massively; paradox of skill; closet indexing. Use index funds for large (and increasingly mid) caps; combine active and passive if desired.

name: Arbitrage Funds
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: At least 65% in hedged arbitrage (mainly cash-futures basis capture, also cross-exchange), rest in debt; equity taxation but debt-like returns (5-7%) - the real arbitrage is tax; not risk-free (debt defaults e.g. DHFL hit, slow recovery); check debt quality and no unhedged equity.

name: Return Measurement (Absolute, CAGR, XIRR, Rolling)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Lump-sum or SIP < 1 yr - absolute return; lump sum > 1 yr - CAGR; SIP > 1 yr - XIRR (cash-flow-dated IRR). Point-to-point returns depend on the two dates; rolling n-year returns (CAGR for every start date) show the distribution - use average, min, max.
formula: {"absolute": "end/start - 1", "cagr": "(end/start) ** (1/years) - 1", "xirr": "rate r s.t. sum(cf_i / (1 + r) ** ((t_i - t_0)/365)) = 0", "rolling_n": "for each date t: (nav_t / nav_{t - n years}) ** (1/n) - 1"}
bot_use: Evaluate strategies with rolling-window returns, not single point-to-point backtests.

name: Expense Ratio (TER) and Direct vs Regular Plans
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: TER is an annual % fee charged daily via NAV; regular plans pay distributor commissions so have higher TER and lower NAV than direct plans - the gap compounds into large differences.

name: Benchmarking and Total Return Index (TRI)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Compare against TRI (price + dividends reinvested), not price index; index returns depend on constituent weights; set realistic personal benchmarks.
bot_use: Benchmark strategies against Nifty 50 TRI.

name: Risk-Adjusted Performance Metrics (Beta, Alpha, SD, Sharpe, Sortino, Capture Ratios)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Beta = relative risk vs benchmark (not inherent risk); alpha = risk-adjusted excess return; SD = inherent volatility; Sharpe = excess return per unit total volatility; Sortino = per unit downside deviation; capture ratios = share of benchmark up/down moves captured - prefer consistent low downside capture.
formula: {"alpha": "(R_fund - Rf) - beta * (R_bench - Rf)", "sharpe": "(R - Rf) / sd", "sortino": "(R - Rf) / downside_deviation", "upside_capture": "fund_return_in_up_periods / bench_return_in_up_periods * 100", "downside_capture": "fund_return_in_down_periods / bench_return_in_down_periods * 100"}
bot_use: Standard strategy scorecard - Sharpe, Sortino, beta/alpha vs Nifty, capture ratios, max drawdown.
caveats: ["Sharpe is meaningless for debt funds (ignores credit/rate risk)."]

name: Analysing Equity and Debt Mutual Funds
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Equity - hygiene (AUM, objective, manager, benchmark) -> 3/5/10-yr rolling returns vs benchmark (avg/min/max) -> risk-return matrix (is excess return from extra risk?) -> capture ratios. Debt - align with goal and horizon, check portfolio credit quality, concentration, duration vs holding period, YTM as risk signal, AUM.

name: Mutual Fund Portfolio Construction
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: First health + term insurance, then emergency corpus; define goal by corpus and time; build by elimination with minimal non-overlapping funds (avoid multiple funds in same subcategory); conservative return assumptions; review yearly; keep it simple.

name: Emergency Corpus
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Second priority after insurance - liquid reserve for unexpected expenses before investing for goals.

name: Smart Beta / Factor Investing
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Smart beta is marketing for factor or alternatively-weighted indices (value, quality, low volatility, momentum etc.); factors are cyclical and can underperform simple index funds for long periods; live fund results differ from index backtests; diversify across factors.

name: Asset Allocation, Sequence Risk and Diversification Vectors
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Prediction is impossible (India beat US 2001-11, reversed next decade) - own a bit of all major assets. Sequence risk - an investor rarely gets average returns; bad years can cluster in your window. Diversify across real drivers (currency, market composition, panic flows - US bonds are safe havens, Indian bonds aren't; avoid bubble assets), not 'diworsification'. Simple start - Indian equity (large-cap index + mid-cap), US equity (cheap S&P 500 fund), short-term govt/PSU bonds, gold (Sovereign Gold Bonds), REITs; equal weight if unsure; stick to the plan.
caveats: ["Financialisation raises correlations between assets (e.g. REITs vs stocks)."]

name: Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs)
type:LABEL: Instrument
summary: Exchange-traded index/commodity/debt wrappers with creation/redemption by market makers/APs; liquidity layers - screen depth, market makers, primary creation, underlying stocks (illiquid underlyings -> premiums/discounts).
conditions: {"always": "use limit orders; compare price with iNAV/underlying index; avoid first 30-60 min after open; check average volumes and tracking vs TRI; prefer AMCs serious about ETFs; create units with AMC for large tickets"}
bot_use: Limit-order execution guard - never market-order an ETF; reject if price deviates from iNAV beyond threshold.
facts: ["ETFs suit tactical/active use of passive exposure; index funds suit set-and-forget."]

name: GDP, Real vs Nominal Growth, and Market Cap
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: GDP = total economic output; real growth = nominal - inflation; India ~$2.6-2.9T (5th/6th, 2020); as GDP grows, aggregate market cap tends to grow - basis for long-term equity investing.

name: Government Finances and Fiscal Deficit
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Revenue = tax (direct - personal/corporate income tax; indirect - GST) + non-tax (PSU dividends, disinvestment); expenditure = revenue (subsidies, salaries, interest) + capital (infrastructure). Fiscal deficit = expenditure - revenue; India FY19 ~3.3% of GDP (govt aims < 4%); higher capex share and tax-to-GDP are positive signals.

name: Systematic Investment Plan (SIP)
type:LABEL: Strategy
summary: Fixed amount invested at fixed intervals (e.g. monthly) into a fund; with annual step-ups it builds long-term corpus; measure SIP returns with XIRR.

name: M13 - Integrated Financial Modelling
type:LABEL: Module
summary: Building an integrated 3-statement Excel model (main model - Bajaj Auto; helper models - Bata etc.) from 5 years of annual-report data - workbook layout, assumption sheet (ratio/growth + rolling averages), revenue sub-model, asset/depreciation, debt and reserves schedules, P&L and balance-sheet projections, indirect cash flow that balances the balance sheet, then valuation (relative, option-based, absolute) via FCFF/FCFE, CAPM, tax shield, WACC, terminal value and DCF to a per-share fair value.

name: Integrated Financial Model
type:LABEL: Model
summary: A linked workbook that takes financial statements as input and outputs a valuation (fair share price); fully integrated, so changing any assumption flows through P&L, balance sheet, cash flow and DCF. Modelling is part art (assumptions) and part craft (structure).
bot_use: Generates a fair value per share and lets you run sensitivity scenarios; feeds margin-of-safety screens and long-horizon value bots. Recompute after every annual/quarterly report.
facts: ["Steps - layout -> historical data (5 yrs, consolidated, from the annual report only) -> assumption sheet -> revenue model -> schedules (asset, debt, reserves) -> P&L/BS projections -> cash flow -> valuation.", "Projection horizon - 5 explicit years (Y6-Y10), then terminal value.", "Pick a simple manufacturing company with 1-2 products and consistent disclosure for a first model; avoid banks/NBFC/BFSI (the model doesn't fit them).", "Sensitivity example - materials consumed 65% -> 60% of sales moved Bajaj Auto fair value from Rs 300 to Rs 462."]

name: Model Layout and Format Hygiene
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Same column = same year across every sheet; narrow index columns A, B and D; no gridlines; freeze panes; units stated (INR Cr); colour-code facts vs assumptions; break heavy line items into detail; do an annual-report recce first and use the latest year's format; never copy from third-party data vendors ('model suicide' = unstructured copy-paste).

name: Assumption Sheet - Ratio/Growth Drivers with Rolling Averages
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Express each line item historically as a ratio to a driver (BS items vs gross block; P&L items vs sales) or as a YoY growth rate; project with the rolling average of the last 4 years (Y6 = avg(Y2..Y5), Y7 = avg(Y3..Y6)) or an informed guess. Prefer drivers with a narrow, stable historical range.
formula: {"ratio_driver": "item_t / driver_t (e.g. liabilities / gross_block)", "growth_driver": "item_t / item_{t-1} - 1", "projection": "item_{t+1} = rolling_mean(ratio, 4) * driver_{t+1}", "deferred_tax": "deferred_tax = avg(deferred_tax / depreciation) * depreciation (more stable than growth)"}

name: Inventory and Receivable Days
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Convert inventory (and receivables) from rupees to days, average the days, then convert back for projections; the days figures also reveal operating efficiency (fewer days = faster conversion to sales).
formula: {"inventory_days": "avg(inventory_{t-1}, inventory_t) / materials_consumed_t * 365", "receivable_days": "avg(receivables_{t-1}, receivables_t) / sales_t * 365", "back_to_value": "inventory_t = inventory_days * materials_consumed_t / 365 (adjusting for averaging)"}

name: Revenue Sub-model
type:LABEL: Model
summary: Build revenue bottom-up from common-sense questions answered in the annual report - what they make, where they sell (domestic vs export), units x realisation per unit, capacity and utilisation. It also yields capacity utilisation, capex cycles and market share.

name: Base Rule (Roll-forward)
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Every schedule rolls forward - this year's closing balance is next year's opening balance; closing = opening + additions - deletions.

name: Asset Schedule (Gross Block, CAPEX, Depreciation, Net Block)
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Back out historical capex from changes in gross block; project capex from management guidance (best), historical averages, or a variable method; project depreciation with the proportion method (depreciation/gross block); roll accumulated depreciation forward; the net block flows back to the balance sheet and the depreciation to the P&L.
formula: {"capex": "gross_block_t - gross_block_{t-1} (+ disposals)", "depreciation_next": "(dep_t / gross_block_t) * gross_block_{t+1}", "accumulated_dep": "acc_dep_{t-1} + dep_t", "net_block": "gross_block - accumulated_depreciation"}

name: Debt Schedule
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Split debt into secured and unsecured using the notes, average the opening and closing balances to get the interest base, and project debt from management's capex/financing view; with no guidance, hold debt flat.

name: Equity / Reserves Schedule
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Share capital (authorised >= issued >= subscribed/paid-up; shares = share capital / face value); reserves - securities premium (rises with fresh equity), general reserve, retained earnings (PAT flows in, dividends and DDT flow out). This is the main P&L-to-BS link.

name: Indirect Cash Flow and Balance Check
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Derive cash flow from P&L and balance-sheet changes - CFO (PAT + depreciation from the asset schedule +/- working-capital changes), CFI (capex, investments), CFF (debt, equity, dividends). Net cash flow plus opening cash gives closing cash, which plugs into the balance sheet; if the model is integrated correctly the balance sheet balances.

name: Valuation Approaches (Relative, Option-based, Absolute)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Relative - value like identical peers via multiples (fails if the sector is mispriced or the companies differ). Option-based - the firm's value depends on an event (e.g. R&D success), valued like an option (niche, tech). Absolute - intrinsic value from discounted cash flow (enterprise or equity). Decision - market price > fair price means overvalued, < means undervalued.
conditions: {"overvalued": "market_price > fair_price", "undervalued": "market_price < fair_price (buy only with margin_of_safety)"}

name: Enterprise Value and Equity Value
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Rearranging the balance sheet - fixed assets = net debt + equity. Valuing the whole firm gives EV (discount FCFF at WACC); EV - debt + cash = equity value; divide by shares outstanding for fair value per share.

name: Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF) and to Equity (FCFE)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: The firm is financed by debt and equity holders; FCFF is the cash available to both, and FCFE is what remains for equity after debt service. Discount FCFF at WACC and FCFE at the cost of equity.
formula: {"fcff_from_pat": "PAT + D&A + interest*(1-tax) + deferred_tax - delta_working_capital - capex", "fcff_from_ebit": "EBIT*(1-tax) + D&A + deferred_tax - delta_working_capital - capex", "fcfe": "FCFF - interest*(1-tax) - principal_repayment + net_new_borrowing", "working_capital": "current_assets - current_liabilities"}

name: Interest Tax Shield / Effective Cost of Debt
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Interest is tax-deductible, so its after-tax cost is lower; add back interest*(1-t) in FCFF and use the after-tax cost of debt in WACC.

name: CAPM - Cost of Equity
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: The return equity holders expect is the risk-free rate plus beta times the market risk premium. Proxy Rf with the 10-year G-sec yield (CCIL/RBI); the long-term market return Rm is ~8-12%.

name: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: A blended discount rate for the whole firm; the cost of equity is always above WACC.

name: Terminal Value (Gordon Growth)
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Beyond the 5 explicit years, assume cash flows grow forever at roughly long-term inflation; DCF is extremely sensitive to this number, and it requires stable positive cash flows (DCF fails with negative ones).
formula: {"tv": "CF_final * (1 + g) / (r - g)", "pv_factor": "1 / (1 + r)^t", "constraint": "r > g; g ~ long-term inflation"}

name: DCF Implementation in the Model
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Inputs are Rf (10Y G-sec, ~7%), Rm (10-12%), beta, kd (~10%), tax (25%), target D/E (50%) and terminal g (~inflation). Steps - project FCFF Y6-Y10, compute TV at Y10, discount everything at WACC, sum to EV, subtract debt and add cash to get equity value, divide by shares for the fair price, then compare with the market price and run sensitivities on key assumptions.
bot_use: fair_value(inputs) -> upside = fair/price - 1; screen for upside > margin_of_safety; run grid sensitivity on g and WACC.

name: M14 - Personal Finance - Insurance
type:LABEL: Module
summary: Health insurance as the first step of a financial plan (authored by Ditto) - honest disclosure, sizing the cover, co-payment and room-rent caps, pre-existing disease waiting periods and loading, specific-illness waiting periods, permanent exclusions, sub-limits and hospital blacklists, floaters, group and employer plans, a gimmick-or-not verdict on common features, claim settlement vs incurred claims ratio, and porting. Indirectly relevant to bots - it protects the trader's capital base, so drawdowns are never forced by medical emergencies.
caveats: ["Product features, waiting periods and IRDAI rules are as of ~2021-22; verify current IRDAI regulations (e.g. moratorium/waiting-period reforms) before relying on numbers."]

name: Insurance (Risk Transfer) - basics
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Insurance transfers the financial risk of rare, high-cost events to an insurer in exchange for a premium; health and term life insurance come before an emergency fund and before investing. Insurers price risk through pooling and are exposed to adverse selection and moral hazard, which explains most policy restrictions.
bot_use: Capital-protection precondition - a trading account should never be the emergency or medical fund.
facts: ["Order of priority - health insurance + term insurance -> emergency corpus -> goal investing.", "Restrictions (waiting periods, co-pay, exclusions) exist to contain customer and hospital abuse."]

name: Health Insurance (Indemnity)
type:LABEL: Product
summary: Pays hospitalisation bills up to the sum insured; the core protection product. Premiums rise every year (~4-6% medical inflation adjustment plus age-band jumps, occasionally regulator-approved repricing) but cannot be raised because you claimed.
facts: ["First 30 days - only accidental hospitalisation is covered.", "Healthcare costs inflate ~6-7%/yr.", "Premium increases are not caused by your own claims (urban myth)."]

name: Full Medical Disclosure (Non-disclosure risk)
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Declare every pre-existing condition and habit directly to the insurer on the proposal form - never rely on an agent's verbal assurance. Non-disclosure lets the insurer repudiate the claim or cancel the policy; a loading charge and a waiting period are far better than a rejected claim.
conditions: {"rule": "disclose all medical history, medication, smoking/alcohol on the form itself"}

name: Perverse Incentives of Agents
type:LABEL: Psychology
summary: Agents earn commission on premium, so they upsell (Rs 50 lakh-1 crore covers via fear) or under-report your conditions to close the sale; evaluate advice by the adviser's incentive.

name: Choosing the Sum Insured
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Most expensive treatments rarely cross ~Rs 20 lakh; a Rs 10-20 lakh base cover (boosted by no-claim bonus and restoration) handles most cases. Rs 5 lakh may be inadequate within a decade given 6-7% medical inflation. A smaller cover is fine for the elderly or if you can't sustain the premium - lapsing a policy is the worst outcome. For rare huge bills, add a super top-up instead of buying a huge base cover.

name: Co-payment Clause
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: You pay a fixed % of every claim (e.g. 20%) in exchange for a lower premium - gives you 'skin in the game'. Usually a bad trade.
conditions: {"avoid_unless": "mandatory, or buying for elderly with pre-existing diseases where it cuts premium sharply"}

name: Room Rent Cap / Proportionate Deduction
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: A cap on room rent (e.g. 1% of sum insured per day). Choosing a costlier room makes the insurer pay proportionately on all room-linked charges (surgeon, consultant, diagnostics), not only the rent difference.
conditions: {"prefer": "no room-rent cap; at least single private room allowed"}

name: Pre-existing Disease (PED) Waiting Period and Loading
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Declared conditions (diabetes, BP, etc.) trigger a PED waiting period (usually 2-4 years) during which related complications aren't covered, and/or a loading charge on the premium (typically 10-20%, up to ~150% for multiple illnesses); insurers may also reject the proposal.

name: Waiting Periods (Initial, Specific Illness, PED)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Three layers - initial 30 days (accidents only); specific-illness list (cataract, stones, deviated septum, hernia, joint replacement etc. - treatments that can be deferred), typically 2 years; PED waiting 2-4 years. Dengue, malaria, fractures, most cancers and heart conditions are covered after 30 days.

name: Permanent Exclusions, Sub-limits, Non-medical Items, Blacklisted Hospitals
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Insurer defences against abuse - permanent exclusions (substance/alcohol-induced illness, cosmetic treatment, external congenital conditions); disease-wise sub-limits (e.g. cardiac Rs 2.5L, knee Rs 2.75L, cataract Rs 50k regardless of cover) - avoid policies with them; non-medical consumables excluded; only 'just and reasonable' treatment per medical council norms paid; blacklisted hospitals can be refused.
conditions: {"check_before_buying": "no disease-wise sub-limits; read permanent exclusion list; check hospital blacklist; get a second opinion for expensive procedures"}

name: Family Floater Policy
type:LABEL: Product
summary: One shared sum insured for self, spouse and children at a discount to individual plans; risks within a family are correlated, so the shared cover can run out. Children must exit after an age limit; parents usually excluded. Online discounts are small (<5% first year); real discounts come from wellness programmes, multi-year tenure or floaters.

name: Group and Employer Health Insurance
type:LABEL: Product
summary: Customised contracts for a group via a master policyholder (bank, employer). Cheaper and often with no waiting periods (invaluable for those with serious PEDs), but pricing is repriced yearly at the insurer's discretion, features are set by the master policyholder, and cover ends if you leave the job or the group dissolves (re-underwriting then). Keep a personal policy alongside an employer cover.
conditions: {"rule": "employer cover + personal base policy (or a super top-up aligned to the employer cover)"}

name: Restoration Benefit
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Restores the sum insured after a claim. Useful in floaters; often neutered by fine print (only for a different illness, or only after the cover is fully exhausted). Verdict - not a gimmick, but buyer beware.

name: No Claim Bonus (NCB)
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Cover grows (e.g. +50% of base) for each claim-free year up to a cap (50%-200% depending on plan); some plans claw it back after a claim, never below base. Verdict - not a gimmick.

name: Health Insurance Features - Gimmick or Not
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: Ditto's verdicts on marketed features.
facts: ["Network hospitals (cashless) - not a gimmick.", "AYUSH cover - slightly gimmicky (only in government-certified AYUSH hospitals with inpatient admission).", "Restoration benefit - not a gimmick, but buyer beware.", "Pre/post hospitalisation (e.g. 30/60 days to 60/180 days) - near-universal, nothing extraordinary.", "Day care (<24h procedures like chemo, dialysis, appendicitis) - not a gimmick; make sure it's covered.", "No claim bonus - not a gimmick.", "Domiciliary cover - slightly gimmicky (needs inability to move / no bed, doctor certification, 72h+).", "Consumables add-on (2-10% of bill) - not a gimmick but touch-and-go; better if bundled with inflation protection.", "Critical illness - slightly gimmicky (narrow severity definitions; a super top-up or term plan does better).", "Top-up - highly gimmicky (deductible applies per hospitalisation).", "Super top-up - not a gimmick, but align policy dates.", "Claim settlement ratio - not a gimmick, but needs context (with ICR).", "Porting - not a gimmick."]

name: Consumables / Non-medical Expenses Add-on
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Gloves, PPE, admin and TV charges are usually excluded (2-10% of a bill); an add-on (~Rs 1,000/yr) covers them. It's marginal unless bundled with inflation protection.

name: Critical Illness Policy
type:LABEL: Product
summary: Covers a listed set of severe diseases, often only at specified severity, and pricing can change sharply. For lump-sum income replacement use term insurance; for medical bills a super top-up is broader. Verdict - slightly gimmicky.

name: Term Life Insurance
type:LABEL: Product
summary: Pure life cover paying a lump sum to dependants on death within the term; the recommended vehicle for lump-sum protection (instead of critical-illness lump sums or investment-linked insurance).

name: Top-up Health Plan
type:LABEL: Product
summary: Large cover above a deductible, but the deductible applies to each hospitalisation separately, so several mid-size bills below the deductible are never paid. Verdict - highly gimmicky.

name: Super Top-up Health Plan
type:LABEL: Product
summary: Very cheap large cover (e.g. Rs 50 lakh for ~Rs 1,000s/yr) that pays once the aggregate bills within a policy year cross the deductible. Choose the deductible equal to the existing base or employer cover, and align policy-year dates with that cover, otherwise the deductible must be met again in a new term.
conditions: {"deductible": "= base/employer cover", "dates": "super top-up renewal aligned with base/employer policy year"}

name: Claim Settlement Ratio (CSR) and Incurred Claims Ratio (ICR)
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: CSR = % of claims settled; it can be gamed (clearing last year's backlog, settling many small claims while rejecting large ones, combining motor/health for general insurers). Read it alongside ICR and scale (large customer base). Get the numbers from the IRDAI annual report.
conditions: {"icr_high": ">100% -> insurer losing money (regulator may force merger)", "icr_low": "~50% -> may be stingy on large claims"}

name: Porting a Health Policy
type:LABEL: Process
summary: Move a policy to a new insurer while carrying over waiting-period credit. Apply 45-60 days before renewal and prove continuous coverage with documents; credit applies only up to the old sum insured (plus bonus) - extra cover serves fresh waiting periods; the new insurer may re-underwrite. Verdict - not a gimmick; usually better than buying fresh.

name: Stop Loss
type:LABEL: Rule
summary: A pre-defined exit price that caps the loss on a trade; placed at a technical level (recent low/high, pattern low) or volatility-based (ATR/SD multiple) and never widened once placed.

name: Dividend Yield
type:LABEL: Ratio
summary: Dividend per share / market price per share; income return of a stock.

name: Quantitative Analysis
type:LABEL: Concept
summary: Systematic, data-driven analysis of prices and fundamentals using statistics; basis of trading systems and backtesting.

name: Pivot Points
type:LABEL: Indicator
summary: Support/resistance levels derived from prior period H/L/C: P=(H+L+C)/3, R1=2P-L, S1=2P-H.

name: Expectancy
type:LABEL: Formula
summary: Average P&L per trade = win_rate * avg_win - loss_rate * avg_loss; a system must have positive expectancy after costs.

name: Trade Execution

name: Averaging Down
